Drug intolerance or drug sensitivity refers to an inability to tolerate the adverse effects of a medication, generally at therapeutic or subtherapeutic doses. Conversely, a patient is said to be "tolerating" a drug when they can tolerate its adverse effects.  Some instances of drug intolerance are known to result from genetic variations in drug metabolism. Pathophysiology
Drugs in systemic circulation have a certain concentration in the blood, which serves as a surrogate marker for how much drug will be delivered throughout the body (how much drug the rest of the body will "see"). There exists a minimum concentration of drug within the blood that will give rise to the intended therapeutic effect (minimum effective concentration, MEC), as well as a minimum concentration of drug that will give rise to an unintended adverse drug event (minimum toxic concentration, MTC). The difference between these two values is generally referred to as the therapeutic window. Different drugs have different therapeutic windows, and different people will have different MECs and MTCs for a given drug. If someone has a very low MTC for a drug, they are likely to experience adverse effects at drug concentrations lower than what it would take to produce the same adverse effects in the general populace; thus, the individual will experience significant toxicity at a dose that is otherwise considered "normal" for the average person. This individual will be considered "intolerant" to that drug.

Gangs of New York is just perfect entertainment. It is an enthralling, bloody, melodramatic epic that more than justifies its two and one half hour running time. In Gangs director Martin Scorsese spins another tale of the New York underworld but with a twist. Instead of the mid-twentieth century organized crime milieu of Goodfellas, Scorsese ventures back to the 19th century to show us the origin of the modern street gang.

It's the early 1860s and the notorious Five Points slum is ruled by the savage `Bill the Butcher'. The viciously nationalistic Bill terrorizes all the immigrant masses jammed into his slum but seems to harbor a particular hatred for the Irish population. Into this seething cauldron wanders mysterious young Amsterdam Vallon who soon works his way into the trust and affection of Bloody Bill. Amsterdam, however, has a past with the unsuspecting Butcher and sports an agenda not unlike a certain Prince of Denmark. Bloody vengeance and dark betrayal soon come to pass, all played against a backdrop of corruption and unrest that lead to up to the horrors of New York Civil War draft riots.

Daniel Day-Lewis is marvelous as Bill the Butcher. His Bill is both recognizably human and a full bore, moustache-twirling villain. Day-Lewis strides his savage and profane way across the screen and steals the whole of the movie. The only other actor to approach Day-Lewis' level is Jim Broadbent as William 'Boss' Tweed. Broadbent is Tweed's spitting image and he makes the grasping old pirate so winning we find ourselves rooting for Tweed against the gaggle of reformers that infest his domain. Though Leonardo DiCaprio is the nominal lead of the picture he is overshadowed by his co-stars. Large, slope shouldered and vaguely brutish looking, DiCaprio is physically perfect for Amsterdam. While he could have used some of the fire and rage of a young James Cagney, DiCaprio's acting is superior throughout the movie. The problem is that Amsterdam just isn't as flashy a role as Bill or Tweed and, as good as DiCaprio is; Day-Lewis operates on a whole other level. Cameron Diaz as the beautiful pickpocket Jenny, never convinces that she is a product of the slums. Despite having considerable screen time, Diaz fades into the background when compared to her more powerful co-stars.

Just as important as the actors are to Gangs is the period atmosphere that drips off the screen. The amazing old New York set has an air of lived in reality that you could cut with a knife. You can almost smell the vermin. Gangs is entirely free of the embalmed feeling you get from most modern period movies. The cast handles the period argot as if it were their true speech and wear their costumes like lived-in clothing. You come away convinced that this is how the world looked and sounded in 1862.

Scorsese does eschew all nuance and subtlety in Gangs. Instead he tells his tale in wide, bold, exploitive and melodramatic strokes that make the movies two and a half hours fly by. Be warned that if you are waiting to see Gangs on DVD you are making a huge mistake. Gangs has to be seen at the theater. The detail and scope of the film cries out to be viewed in all its wide screen glory. This movie is a fantastic achievement.

text:
In this paper, we explore the connection between supersymmetry and the topology of the eigensurface of the spherical quantum pendulum. The spherical quantum pendulum is a quantum mechanical system that has been shown to exhibit rich and interesting properties, including the presence of exceptional points, where the system's energy levels coalesce and the usual quantum mechanical phenomenon of level repulsion is violated.

By employing a combination of algebraic and geometric techniques, we demonstrate that the eigensurface of the spherical quantum pendulum can be endowed with a supersymmetric structure. This supersymmetry is found to be related to the topological properties of the eigensurface, specifically its non-trivial topology, which is characterized by a non-vanishing fundamental group.

We show that the supersymmetry of the eigensurface of the spherical quantum pendulum is intimately connected to the presence of exceptional points in the system's energy spectrum. The exceptional points are found to be related to the zeroes of the Witten index, which is a topological invariant that characterizes the supersymmetry of the system.

Our results provide new insights into the relationship between supersymmetry and topology in the context of quantum mechanics. They also shed light on the role of exceptional points in the physics of quantum systems, and highlight the potential of supersymmetry as a tool for understanding the behavior of quantum systems in regimes where traditional methods are inadequate.

Overall, our work demonstrates the power of algebraic and geometric techniques in the study of quantum systems, and opens up new avenues for exploring the interplay between supersymmetry, topology, and quantum mechanics.

prompt: Write the body of a BBC news article titled "Concern over RFID tags". Do not repeat the title.
text:
A growing number of consumer protection groups are expressing concern about the use of Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) tags in everyday products. Experts say these tags, mostly used for stock control, could potentially endanger consumer privacy and increase cybersecurity risks. 

RFID tags, tiny electronic devices typically packed into stickers or embedded into plastic, are commonly used for tracking and identification purposes in a wide range of industries. For instance, retailers use them to track inventory and manage supply chains, while vets use them to identify pets. 

Increasingly, however, these potentially invasive devices are finding their way into personal belongings, like clothing and accessories, sparking fears that they could be used to collect customer data without consent. Privacy concern arises especially when these RFID tags continue to remain active even after completing a purchase, presenting a possibility of tracking consumers without their knowledge. 

Data protection advocates argue that the indiscriminate use of RFID tags represents a significant breach of privacy. Dr Alan Simpson, a cybersecurity expert from Nottingham Trent University, said: "RFID tags, if not properly secured or deactivated, can expose consumers to unwanted tracking and profiling."

At the same time, critics highlight the risk of criminals exploiting such technology. They warn that cybercriminals who gain access to RFID-tagged data can use it for different types of fraud or identity theft. 

In response to the increasing concern, a spokesperson for the RFID Journal, a publication dedicated to the RFID industry, commented: "RFID technology is merely a tool. Like any tool, it's the way it's used that determines whether it's beneficial or harmful. Many RFID vendors offer tags that can be killed permanently or encrypted for additional security."

Meanwhile, some argue that legislation has not kept pace with the evolution of technology. No universal laws are governing the usage and data handling aspects of RFID technology. According to Dr Simpson, "there is a pressing need for a comprehensive review of existing regulations concerning RFID use."

In November last year, the European Institute for Privacy and Data Protection published a report calling for pan-European guidelines on the use of RFID technology, suggesting that the issue might soon receive legislative attention.

While RFID technology continues to revolutionise commercial industries and offer significant benefits in areas like supply chain management, growing concern over privacy and data protection may hinder its widespread acceptance.

The RFID industry finds itself at the crossroads, facing the challenge of addressing privacy concerns and cybersecurity vulnerabilities, without compromising the benefits RFID technology can provide to businesses. Future regulatory discussions will indeed determine the trajectory of this contentious technology.

prompt: Write the abstract for the academic paper titled "Customizable Architecture Search for Semantic Segmentation".
text: Semantic segmentation is an important task in computer vision that involves partitioning an image into meaningful regions. Traditional deep learning-based approaches for semantic segmentation rely on pre-trained architectures and fixed hyperparameters. However, these methods often fail to take into account the unique characteristics of specific image datasets, leading to suboptimal results. Customizable Architecture Search (CAS) addresses this issue by providing a framework for automatically searching and selecting the best architecture for a given task. This paper presents CAS for semantic segmentation, which utilizes a subset of the standard convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture to search for the optimal combination of layers and hyperparameters. The results show that CAS significantly outperforms fixed architectures on several benchmark datasets, achieving state-of-the-art performance on some tasks. Furthermore, CAS also provides interpretable explanations for its decisions, allowing researchers to understand the factors that contribute to the success of different architectures. Overall, this work demonstrates the potential of CAS for improving the performance of deep learning-based semantic segmentation.

prompt: Write a recipe for "Spiced Turkey Sliders With Caramelized Onions & Apples".
text:
Ingredients:
- 1 lb ground turkey
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 teaspoon garlic powder
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 1 large onion, thinly sliced
- 2 apples, thinly sliced
- 2 tablespoons brown sugar
- 2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar
- 12 slider buns

Instructions:
1. Preheat your grill or stovetop grill pan to medium-high heat.
2. In a medium bowl, combine the ground turkey, olive oil, smoked paprika, garlic powder, ground cumin, ground cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Mix well with your hands until all the ingredients are evenly incorporated.
3. Divide the turkey mixture into 12 equal portions and shape into small patties.
4. Place the turkey patties on the preheated grill or grill pan and cook for about 4-5 minutes per side or until cooked through and internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C).
5. While the turkey is cooking, heat a large skillet over medium heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Add the sliced onions and cook, stirring occasionally, for about 8-10 minutes or until golden brown and caramelized.
6. Push the onions to one side of the skillet and add the sliced apples. Sprinkle the brown sugar over the apples and cook for another 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the apples are tender and caramelized as well.
7. Pour the apple cider vinegar into the skillet with the onions and apples and toss everything together. Cook for another 1-2 minutes to allow the flavors to meld together.
8. To assemble the sliders, slice the buns in half and place a turkey patty on the bottom half of each bun. Top with a spoonful of the caramelized onions and apples mixture, and cover with the top half of the bun.
9. Serve the spiced turkey sliders immediately, and you can garnish with additional toppings like lettuce, tomato slices, or your favorite condiments if desired.
10. Enjoy these delicious and flavorful spiced turkey sliders with caramelized onions and apples!

While doing some research before reviewing 1408, I was shocked to discover that this was the first time since 2004's Riding the Bullet that a film based on a Stephen King story had gotten the big screen treatment. 1408 marks somewhat of a comeback to the silver screen for the author after mainly working with television the past couple years. Director Mikael Hafstrom has created the most atmospheric and downright tense thriller I can think of so far this year. The premise may be thin, and yeah, it doesn't always make a lot of sense. But, is it ever effective.

Mike Enslin (John Cusack) used to be a promising author until the untimely death of his young daughter, Katie (Jasmine Jessica Anthony). He now spends his time writing trashy paranormal novels about the world's most haunted areas. He travels the world, doing research by staying overnight at places that are supposed to be haunted, gets some colorful background info that he can use for material, and then moves on to his next job. One day, Mike receives a postcard informing him of an old hotel in New York City called the Dolphin Hotel, which is supposed to have a room that has quite the history. Doing some private research, he learns that the Dolphin has had a long and tragic history of deaths, all of them surrounding the guests that have stayed in Room 1408. Mike books the room, despite the warnings of the hotel manager, Gerald Olin (Samuel L.Jackson). Entering the room, nothing seems ominous at first. But then, the room itself begins to take on a life of its own, and begins tormenting Mike with various ghostly apparitions, mind tricks, and even displaying his own painful past before him in various ways.

1408 is the second thriller set around a hotel released in less than two months (the other being April's Vacancy), and is by far the superior film. The film is actually quite subtle in its way of creeping us out and disturbing us, which is a nice change of pace from the recent Hostel: Part II. Rather than bombard the audience with ghostly special effects and gore, the movie gets under your skin and goes for a much more psychological approach. The screenplay by Matt Greenberg, Scott Alexander, and Larry Karaszewski, wisely does not even attempt to explain Room 1408. It's just a very evil presence that can somehow look deep within troubled souls, and torture them to death with their own personal demons. In the wrong hands, this material could have been laughable. Even though the movie frequently flies into the realm of the unbelievable, it manages to somehow stay grounded.

A lot of this has to do with the fact that the film never loses its way, and become an excuse to throw as many special effects and jump scares into the movie as it possibly can. The human element of Mike Enslin is always at the center of the story itself, and its scares. The movie is built around the fact that he is forced to face his personal demons the longer he stays in his room, as well as try to keep his mind in check as various nightmarish hallucinations are paraded before him. It's much more effective than the usual characters that have passed as villains in recent paranormal films (usually gray-skinned people with hair over their faces), and it never once becomes heavy-handed or preachy. This is also a tricky balance to pull off. When the room started showing him flashbacks of Mike's own past, I grew nervous, thinking that the movie was going to start hitting us over the head with morales. Fortunately, it never once loses its sense of the eerie, and remains appropriately unsettling throughout.

At the center of the movie is John Cusack, who literally has to carry the movie almost by himself. This is essentially a one-man show for most of its running time, with fleeting apparitions being his main companions. Cusack has long been a favorite of mine, and this is one of his stronger recent roles. He not only has to carry almost the entire film on his own, but he also has to convincingly act like he is slowly going insane without hamming it up, or losing his personality. Any actor can tell you that madness is a difficult thing to depict. He strikes a very good balance, and remains believable throughout. Samuel L. Jackson is also notable in his small, but no less important, role as the manager who tries to talk Mike out of his decision to stay in the room. And then, of course, there is Room 1408, which is a character itself. The way it is constantly changing itself, right down to the paintings on the wall, creates an effectively creepy atmosphere that is continuously bizarre, but never so much so that we lose our sense to believe.

1408 succeeds where so many other films have failed in that it is not about apparitions jumping out at the actors or lurking in dark shadows. It digs much deeper for its horror than simple jolt thrills, and becomes an effectively thrilling horror film. It could be argued that the whole thing loses some weight when we apply logic to the story. But seriously, who wants to apply logic to a movie about an evil hotel room that can read your mind? When all is said and done, 1408 is a reminder of what horror can do. It can do so much more than thrill us. It can also make us laugh and leave us captivated. Perhaps what's more surprising than the fact that the movie can accomplish all that is that so few other horror films can.

text:
Live streaming is a process of broadcasting video or audio content in real-time over the internet. While the concept is relatively simple, the technical processes behind it can be more complex. Here is an overview of how live streaming works:

1. Capture the content: To live stream, you need to capture the video or audio content you want to share. This can be done using a camera or microphone, depending on the type of content you are streaming.
2. Encode the content: Once the content is captured, it needs to be encoded. Encoding compresses the content into a format that can be transmitted over the internet. There are several different encoding standards and techniques that can be used, but the most common are H.264 and MPEG-4.
3. Choose a streaming platform: There are many different platforms available for live streaming, including Twitch, YouTube, Facebook, and more. Each platform has its own features and capabilities, so it's important to choose one that meets your needs.
4. Setup the stream: Once you have chosen a platform, you will need to set up the stream. This typically involves creating an account, configuring your settings, and setting up any necessary equipment.
5. Start streaming: When you are ready to start streaming, simply launch your platform and begin broadcasting your content. Your viewers will be able to watch the stream in real-time through their internet connection.

Overall, live streaming is a simple and accessible way to share content with others. By following these steps, you can begin streaming in no time.

I was invited to a screening of The Peaceful Warrior in NYC Thursday April 13th, having just learned of this film's existence a few days earlier.

I was looking forward to the film, but with some trepidation, considering that prior attempts at communicating spiritually oriented books or ideas had fallen short of my expectations and had fundamentally failed to convey to the audience a transforming inner experience; witness What the Bleep, Siddhartha, Little Buddha, and others.

Let me say this, simply and directly. They got it right this time, and they did it in a way which could be embraced by crowds at the multiplexes. By impressing the discovery of bona fide spiritual truths on a recognizable sports template, the movie makers will be carrying under-appreciated ideas and experiences to the masses. At least I hope so! I actually woke up early the morning after seeing this, with my mind full of things I might say in an exhaustive review. Never in my life have I felt that way about a movie before.

The reason this movie succeeds is that it follows one of the most basic rules for good story-telling: it shows rather than tells. Although some fundamental spiritual ideas are described with words, it is the plot and character development that proves the truth of those words. You see the transcendence and the realizations in the faces of the characters, and you are not left to wonder why. You understand.

The story, based on a book by Dan Millman, follows a college gymnast who has great potential but whose desire for success is one of the main obstacles standing in the way of that potential. In his mindless pursuit of a goal, he becomes sucked into the deep dark hole of life-is-what-happens-while-you're-making-other-plans. In its simplest message, our hero's real challenge is to find happiness by being present and finding interest and love for what's right in front of him.

The film doesn't try to oversimplify the content of a spiritual path into a single dogma; there are many other seeds of thought strewn along the path by Socrates, each of which could have been the basis for a different struggle to transcend relative unconsciousness.

For many years I have been convinced that non-religious spiritual thought and experience could be something to drive the world in a new direction. This movie provides an example of what life can be like if we ponder these thoughts and implement them in our lives in a concrete and practical way. It's not necessary to be a champion gymnast to derive the fundamental teachings from this film. It is a teaching that anyone can understand. This is why I see that The Peaceful Warrior can inspire those who embrace the possibilities which it offers to become peaceful guerrilla warriors, working tirelessly underneath the radar, changing the world.

This is not only a good movie, it's an important one.

Domain adaptation (DA) has drawn high interest for its capacity to adapt a
model trained on labeled source data to perform well on unlabeled or weakly
labeled target data from a different domain. Most common DA techniques require
concurrent access to the input images of both the source and target domains.
However, in practice, privacy concerns often impede the availability of source
images in the adaptation phase. This is a very frequent DA scenario in medical
imaging, where, for instance, the source and target images could come from
different clinical sites. We introduce a source-free domain adaptation for
image segmentation. Our formulation is based on minimizing a label-free entropy
loss defined over target-domain data, which we further guide with a
domain-invariant prior on the segmentation regions. Many priors can be derived
from anatomical information. Here, a class ratio prior is estimated from
anatomical knowledge and integrated in the form of a Kullback Leibler (KL)
divergence in our overall loss function. Furthermore, we motivate our overall
loss with an interesting link to maximizing the mutual information between the
target images and their label predictions. We show the effectiveness of our
prior aware entropy minimization in a variety of domain-adaptation scenarios,
with different modalities and applications, including spine, prostate, and
cardiac segmentation. Our method yields comparable results to several state of
the art adaptation techniques, despite having access to much less information,
as the source images are entirely absent in our adaptation phase. Our
straightforward adaptation strategy uses only one network, contrary to popular
adversarial techniques, which are not applicable to a source-free DA setting.
Our framework can be readily used in a breadth of segmentation problems, and
our code is publicly available: https://github.com/mathilde-b/SFDA

challenging in connectomics. Recent advances in deep learning have demonstrated
the significant potential of automatic segmentation for tera-scale EM images.
However, none of the existing segmentation methods are error-free, and they
require proofreading, which is typically implemented as an interactive,
semi-automatic process via manual intervention. Herein, we propose a fully
automatic proofreading method based on reinforcement learning. The main idea is
to model the human decision process in proofreading using a reinforcement agent
to achieve fully automatic proofreading. We systematically design the proposed
system by combining multiple reinforcement learning agents in a hierarchical
manner, where each agent focuses only on a specific task while preserving
dependency between agents. Furthermore, we also demonstrate that the episodic
task setting of reinforcement learning can efficiently manage a combination of
merge and split errors concurrently presented in the input. We demonstrate the

prompt: Write a recipe for "Quick Clam Chowder".
text:
Recipe for "Quick Clam Chowder"

Ingredients:
- 2 cans of canned clams in juice
- 2 strips of bacon, diced
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 1 cup of diced celery
- 2 medium potatoes, cubed
- 1 cup of water
- 1 cup of half and half or heavy cream
- 1 teaspoon of salt
- 1/2 teaspoon of black pepper
- 1 garlic clove, minced
- 2 tablespoons of flour
- 2 tablespoons of butter

Instructions:

1. Saute the chopped bacon in a large saucepan over medium heat until it's crisp. Remove the bacon and set it aside.

2. Drain off most of the bacon grease, leaving about 2 tablespoons in the pan. Add the minced garlic, chopped onion, celery, and cubed potatoes to the saucepan, and saute until the onions become translucent. Be careful to not burn them.

3. Sprinkle flour over the vegetables and stir for a couple of minutes to create a roux. The roux will act as your thickening agent. 

4. Slowly add the water and clam juice that come from the canned clams, stirring constantly to keep the smooth texture. 

5. Cover the pan and let it simmer over low heat, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes are tender. It should take about 15 mins.

6. Once the potatoes are cooked, add the clams and stir to combine. Simmer for another 2 minutes.

7. Turn the heat down to low, then add the half and half or heavy cream, butter as well as the cooked bacon. Stir until the butter is melted and incorporated.

8. Season the chowder with salt and pepper. Taste it and adjust the seasonings as needed.

9. Cook over low heat for about 5 more minutes, or until the chowder is hot. Stir occasionally to prevent it from sticking.

10. Your Quick Clam Chowder is ready! Serve it piping hot with a side of crusty bread
   

Note:
- Do not boil it after adding the cream to prevent curdling.
- You can also add herbs like thyme or parsley for extra flavor.

text:
The 1906 World Series was a prestigious event in the history of American baseball, marking the second ever modern World Series to be played. Held from October 9th to October 14th, the series was a best-of-seven playoff that saw the Chicago White Sox emerging as the champion over their cross-town rivals, the Chicago Cubs. This was the only World Series that featured two teams from the same city until the New York Giants and the New York Yankees faced off in 1921, and remains one of only 11 series in which the teams hail from the same city.

Nicknamed "The Hitless Wonders," the White Sox finished 93-58 in the regular season, despite having the weakest hitting in the American League. This title was due to their .230 batting average throughout the season, which was the worst for a championship team in the history of American League. The team, however, demonstrated commendable fielding and outstanding pitching throughout the series.

On the other hand, the Cubs came into the series after completing one of the greatest regular seasons in baseball history. They finished with a remarkable record of 116-36, which remains the highest single-season win percentage (.763) in Major League history. The Cubs were favorites entering the contest, but were unable to carry their regular season dominance into the World Series.

The series is most remembered for the stunning upset by the White Sox. Despite having a far superior hitting average than the White Sox, the Cubs were outplayed over six games, with the final game witnessing a victorious 8-3 score for the White Sox, marking their first World Series championship. Ed Walsh of the White Sox earned two wins during this series and hit .364 in the six games.

The 1906 World Series is noteworthy as it highlights the unpredictable nature of baseball. Despite a seemingly inferior team on paper, the White Sox were able to pull off a significant upset, demonstrating that any team has the potential to triumph, regardless of regular-season statistics. This concept continues to resonate in contemporary baseball, where the playoffs are known for their unpredictability.

The aftermath of the series saw the White Sox gain a significant boost in popularity in Chicago and across the nation, whereas the Cubs became infamous for their inability to maintain their regular-season dominance in the post-season, a legacy that would haunt the team for the following century until their ultimate World Series win in 2016.

Anglicanism is a Western Christian tradition that has developed from the practices, liturgy, and identity of the Church of England following the English Reformation, in the context of the Protestant Reformation in Europe. It is one of the largest branches of Christianity, with around 110 million adherents worldwide . Adherents of Anglicanism are called Anglicans; they are also called Episcopalians in some countries. The majority of Anglicans are members of national or regional ecclesiastical provinces of the international Anglican Communion, which forms the third-largest Christian communion in the world, after the Roman Catholic Church and the Eastern Orthodox Church. These provinces are in full communion with the See of Canterbury and thus with the British Monarch’s personal choice of the Archbishop of Canterbury, whom the communion refers to as its primus inter pares (Latin, 'first among equals'). The Archbishop calls the decennial Lambeth Conference, chairs the meeting of primates, and is the president of the Anglican Consultative Council. Some churches that are not part of the Anglican Communion or recognised by it also call themselves Anglican, including those that are within the Continuing Anglican movement and Anglican realignment.

prompt: Write the abstract for the academic paper titled "TFLMS: Large Model Support in TensorFlow by Graph Rewriting".
text: This paper introduces TensorFlow Large Model Support (TFLMS), a novel approach to managing the memory requirements of large models and data during deep learning model training using TensorFlow. It addresses the inability of TensorFlow to handle models with memory sizes larger than the capacity of GPU memory. We propose TFLMS, which uses various graph rewriting techniques to modify the TensorFlow computation graph. This makes it possible to split large models into smaller sub-models that fit into GPU memory and supports training data to be swapped in and out of the GPU memory as needed. We compared the performance of using TFLMS to non-TFLMS and explored the impacts of different factors such as batch size, model size, and input shape on the speedup. Our results indicate that TFLMS can effectively train large models on GPUs and significantly reduce out-of-memory errors.

- 2 teaspoons ground cinnamon
- 1 teaspoon ground nutmeg

- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar
- 2 tablespoons brown sugar
- Salt to taste

text:
Ingredients:

- 2 large eggplants, cut into 1 inch circles
- 3 cups of tomato passata (pureed tomatoes)
- 2 cloves of garlic, minced
- 2 cups of flour
- 3 large eggs
- 3 cups of bread crumbs
- Basil leaves
- 1 1/2 cup Parmigiano-Reggiano, finely grated
- 2 cups mozzarella cheese, shredded
- Sea salt and black pepper
- Extra-virgin olive oil

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 350°F. In the meantime, generously salt the eggplant slices and let them drain in a colander. This will remove any excess moisture and bitterness from the eggplant.

2. While the eggplant is draining, prepare the tomato sauce. In a large skillet, heat a tablespoon of olive oil over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and cook until fragrant. Add the tomato passata and season with some salt and pepper. Let it simmer for about 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Set aside when done.

3. Rinney the eggplant slices, pat them dry, and start preparing the breading station. You will need one bowl for the flour, one for the beaten eggs, and one for the bread crumbs. 

4. Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and drizzle with olive oil. In small batches, dip the eggplant slices first in the flour to coat, then in the egg, and lastly in the bread crumbs to coat. Fry them until they turn golden brown on both sides. Transfer the fried slices to a paper towel-lined plate to drain off any excess oil.

5. After frying all the eggplant slices, start layering your eggplant parmesan in a baking dish. Start with a layer of tomato sauce, then a layer of eggplant slices, followed by a sprinkle of both cheeses and a few basil leaves. Repeat these layers until all your ingredients are used up, finishing with a layer of cheese on top.

6. Bake in the preheated oven for about 30 minutes, or until bubbling and golden brown on top. 

7. Let the eggplant parmesan cool for a few minutes before serving. Sprinkle with some fresh basil and extra Parmigiano-Reggiano, if desired. Enjoy your delicious Eggplant Parmesan: Parmigiana di Melanzane a la Mario Batali!

- 1 tablespoon sake
- 1 tablespoon grated ginger 
- 1 tablespoon minced garlic 
- 1/2 cup potato starch or corn starch 
- Oil for deep frying 
- Lemon wedges and Japanese mayonnaise for serving 

Instructions: 

1. Cut the chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces.

8. Deep fry the chicken in batches, being careful not to overcrowd the pan. Remove the chicken when golden brown, typically this takes about 3-4 minutes. 

9. Leave the chicken to drain on sieve or kitchen paper to remove any excess oil.

11. Serve the chicken karaage hot with lemon wedges and Japanese mayonnaise.

prompt: Write a recipe for "Chococonut Pandan Chiffon Cake".
text:
Recipe: Chococonut Pandan Chiffon Cake

Ingredients:
- 6 egg yolks
- 1 cup all-purpose flour
- 1/2 cup sugar
- 1/2 teaspoon pandan flavoring
- 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract
- 1/4 cup vegetable oil
- 1/4 cup coconut milk
- 1/4 cup hot water
- 1/4 cup cocoa powder
- 1/2 teaspoon baking powder
- 1/4 teaspoon salt
- 6 egg whites
- 1/4 teaspoon cream of tartar
- 1/2 cup sugar

Instructions:

1. Preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C). Grease and flour a 10-inch chiffon cake pan.

2. In a large mixing bowl, combine the egg yolks, sugar, pandan flavoring, and vanilla extract. Mix until well combined.

3. In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, cocoa powder, baking powder, and salt.

4. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the egg yolk mixture, alternating with the vegetable oil, coconut milk, and hot water. Mix until the batter is smooth and well combined.

5. In another mixing bowl, beat the egg whites and cream of tartar until frothy. Gradually add the sugar and continue beating until stiff peaks form.

6. Gently fold the beaten egg whites into the cake batter in three additions, using a spatula. Be careful not to overmix so as not to deflate the egg whites.

7. Pour the batter into the prepared cake pan and smooth the top with a spatula.

8. Bake for approximately 45-50 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean.

9. Once baked, remove the cake from the oven and invert the pan onto a wire rack. Let the cake cool completely in the pan.

10. Once the cake has cooled, run a knife around the sides of the pan to release the cake. Gently tap the pan to loosen the cake from the bottom and carefully remove the cake from the pan.

11. Serve the chococonut pandan chiffon cake as is or dust it with powdered sugar for added decoration. Enjoy!

Note: Store any leftovers in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days.

prompt: Write a recipe for "Better-Than-Panera Honey-Wheat Bread".
text:
Ingredients:

For the Dough:
- 1 1/2 cups warm water
- 3 tablespoons honey
- 1 1/2 teaspoons salt
- 2 1/2 cups whole wheat flour
- 1 cup bread flour
- 3 tablespoons butter, softened
- 1/2 cup rolled oats
- 2 1/4 teaspoons active dry yeast

For the Glaze:
- 2 tablespoons honey
- 1 tablespoon water

Instructions:

1. In a large bowl, mix together warm water and honey until honey is dissolved.
2. Add salt, whole wheat flour, bread flour, softened butter, oats, and active dry yeast to the honey-water mixture. Mix until the ingredients are well-combined and form a dough. The dough should be slightly sticky. 

3. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for about 10 minutes, until the dough is smooth and elastic.
   
4. Shape the dough into a ball and place it in a greased large bowl, turning it to coat all sides with the grease. Cover the bowl with a clean cloth and allow it to rise in a warm place for about 1 hour, or until it doubles in size.
   
5. Punch down the dough and turn it out onto a lightly floured surface. Shape it into a loaf by rolling it into a rectangle, then rolling it up tightly, starting from a short end. Pinch the seams to seal.

6. Place the loaf in a greased 9x5 inch loaf pan with the seam side down. Cover and let it rise until doubled, about 1 hour.

7. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).

8. For the glaze: mix together honey and water. Brush this mixture over the top of the risen loaf.

9. Bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and the loaf sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom. 

10. Remove from the oven and immediately remove from pan to cool completely on a wire rack.

Enjoy your homemade honey-wheat bread that's even better than Panera's! It is perfect for sandwiches, toast, or simply spread with butter.

prompt: Write a recipe for "Chicken Fingers Parmesan".
text:
Ingredients:
- 2 lbs chicken tenderloins or chicken breast strips
- 1 cup all-purpose flour
- 2 large eggs
- 2 cups panko bread crumbs
- 1 cup Parmesan cheese, freshly grated
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 1 cup marinara sauce
- 1 cup mozzarella cheese, shredded
- 2 tbsp fresh basil, chopped (optional)
- Olive oil, for frying

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 375F (190C).

2. Season the chicken tenders with salt and pepper. 

3. Prepare your breading station: In one bowl, place the flour. In a second bowl, beat the eggs. In a third bowl, combine the panko bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, oregano, and a pinch of salt and pepper. 

4. Dredge each chicken tender in the flour, shaking off any excess. Then dip it into the beaten eggs, and finally press it into the breadcrumb mixture. Make sure the chicken is thoroughly coated in each layer.

5. Heat about 1/2 inch of olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Once the oil is hot, add the chicken tenders in batches, taking care not to overcrowd the pan. 

6. Cook each side for about 3-4 minutes, until golden brown and crispy. Once done, transfer the chicken fingers onto a paper towel-lined plate to drain off any excess oil.

7. Place the fried chicken fingers on a baking tray. Spoon marinara sauce over each tender, then sprinkle generously with shredded mozzarella cheese.

8. Bake in the preheated oven for about 10-15 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly.

9. (Optional) Sprinkle with fresh chopped basil before serving. 

10. Serve your chicken fingers parmesan with pasta, salad, or a side of your choice. Enjoy!

This recipe serves 4 to 6 individuals. It can be a tasty lunch or dinner option for children and adults alike. Enjoy this delicious spin on a classic favorite!

Floyd Alburn Firestone (1898–1986) was an acoustical physicist, who in 1940 while a professor at the University of Michigan invented the first practical ultrasonic testing method and apparatus. He was granted US Patent 2,280,226 for the invention in 1942. Manufactured by Sperry Corporation, the testing device was known variously as the Firestone-Sperry Reflectoscope, the Sperry Ultrasonic Reflectoscope, the Sperry Reflectoscope and sometimes also just as a Supersonic Reflectoscope, the name Firestone had originally coined for the instrument. The technology is not just used in quality control in factories to reject defective parts before shipment, but also revolutionized transportation safety. For example, ultrasonic testing is used for safety maintenance inspection of railroad cars, particularly axles and wheels, aircraft, particularly fuselages, and other transportation vessels for material fatigue. Dr. Firestone’s ultrasonic pulse echo technique for metal defect testing was also later applied in medical diagnosis, giving birth to the field of Echocardiography and to the field of Medical Ultrasonography, generally. Dr. Firestone was the editor of the Journal of the Acoustical Society of America from 1939-1957. Among Firestone’s many other inventions in his field are in a single year an “automatic device for the minute inspection of flaws”, “a new and useful improvement in hook-up of electrical apparatus”, and “[a] device for measuring noise”, and, even, later a “musical typewriter”. In 1933, Firestone proposed an alternative to the mechanical–electrical analogy of James Clerk Maxwell in which force is made the analogy of voltage (the impedance analogy).  Firestone's analogy (now called the mobility analogy) makes force the analogy of current.  In this work he introduced the concept of "through" and "across" variables and demonstrated that there were analogies for these variables in other energy domains, making it possible to treat a complex system as a unified whole in analysis.  Firestone's analogy became popular amongst mechanical filter designers because it has the property of preserving network topologies when transforming between the mechanical and electrical domains.

text:
Expansion path refers to the path taken by a firm in its production process as it expands its output. It illustrates the optimal combination of inputs, such as labor and capital, as a firm increases its scale of production. The expansion path depicts the relationship between the firm's input choices and its level of output.

As a firm expands its production, it can choose different combinations of inputs depending on its technological capabilities, cost structures, and factor prices. The expansion path shows how a firm can maintain its cost-minimizing input combination while increasing its output.

In the short run, a firm may choose to expand its output by employing more labor while keeping its capital stock constant. This is known as labor-intensive expansion, as it relies more on labor as the primary input. However, as the scale of production increases, the firm may reach a point where additional labor alone cannot support its expanding output. At this stage, the firm may need to increase its capital stock to achieve further growth, resulting in a capital-intensive expansion.

The shape and slope of the expansion path depend on various factors, including the substitutability and complementarity between inputs, the elasticity of substitution, and the technology used by the firm. In general, the expansion path is upward sloping, reflecting the increasing returns to scale as the firm grows. However, the slope may vary at different stages of expansion depending on the specific production conditions.

The expansion path concept is often used in economic analysis to understand the behavior of firms in response to changes in their production scale. By analyzing the expansion path, economists can evaluate the efficiency and cost implications of a firm's production decisions. It provides insights into the optimal allocation of resources and the trade-offs involved in production expansion.

In addition to its application in economic analysis, the concept of expansion path is also relevant in business strategy and decision-making. Firms can use the expansion path model to plan their growth strategies, considering the most efficient use of inputs, the scale of operations, and the potential cost savings associated with expansion.

Overall, the expansion path concept is a fundamental tool for understanding the dynamics of firm expansion and the relationship between input choices and output levels. It provides valuable insights into the efficient allocation of resources and the trade-offs involved in production scalability.

text:
Lemon Curd Tart with French Meringue

Ingredients:

For the tart:

* 1 unbaked 9-inch tart crust, either homemade or store-bought
* 2 large eggs
* 3/4 cup granulated sugar
* 3 tablespoons unsalted butter, softened
* 1/2 cup fresh lemon juice
* 1 tablespoon lemon zest

For the French meringue:

* 3 large egg whites
* 1/2 teaspoon salt
* 2/3 cup granulated sugar

Instructions:

1. Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
2. In a medium bowl, whisk together the eggs and granulated sugar until light and fluffy.
3. Melt the butter in a small saucepan, then transfer it to a heatproof bowl. Gradually pour the melted butter into the egg mixture, whisking constantly, until fully incorporated.
4. Add the lemon juice and zest to the egg mixture and stir to combine.
5. Pour the lemon curd into the prepared tart crust and smooth the surface with a spatula. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the filling is set and the crust is lightly browned on top. Allow the tart to cool completely before refrigerating it.
6. To make the meringue, beat the egg whites and salt in a large bowl until stiff peaks form. Gradually add the sugar, one tablespoon at a time, and continue to beat until the sugar dissolves and the meringue is glossy and stiff.
7. Spoon the meringue onto the cooled tart, using the back of the spoon to shape the meringue peaks.
8. Return the tart to the oven and bake for an additional 10-15 minutes, or until the meringue is lightly browned and the filling is heated through. Serve the tart immediately and enjoy!

text:
Made-to-measure (MTM) is a clothing manufacturing method where garments are made to the exact measurements of each individual customer. This bespoke tailoring technique involves taking detailed measurements of a person's body, and using those measurements to create a garment that fits perfectly. The result is a high-quality, custom-fit garment that can provide superior comfort, durability, and style.

The MTM process typically involves the following steps:

1. Measurement: The first step is to take accurate measurements of the customer's body. This may involve the use of specialized measuring tools such as tape measures, rulers, or 3D scanners. The measurements are typically taken at key points on the body such as the chest, waist, hips, and arms, and may also include measurements of the inseam, shoulder width, and sleeve length.
2. Pattern Making: Once the measurements have been taken, a pattern is created based on the individual's body shape and size. This pattern is then used to create a garment that is precisely tailored to the customer's dimensions.
3. Cutting: Once the pattern has been created, the fabric is carefully cut to the pattern lines. This requires a high degree of precision and skill, as any mistakes can result in wasted fabric or an ill-fitting garment.
4. Sewing: The pieces of fabric are then sewn together using high-quality thread and needles. The seams are carefully reinforced and finished to ensure that the garment is both durable and comfortable.
5. Alterations: If necessary, the garment may require some alterations to ensure that it fits perfectly. This may involve adjustments to the pattern, alterations to the fabric, or both.

Made-to-measure clothing can be created for a wide range of garments, including suits, dresses, shirts, pants, and more. The process can be time-consuming and expensive, but the result is a garment that is perfectly tailored to the individual's body and preferences. For some people, the investment in a high-quality made-to-measure garment is well worth the cost, as it can provide superior comfort and style for years to come.

text:
Many of our social interactions, be it physical or digital, revolve around communication and sharing our thoughts and opinions. The beautiful part about these interactions is the variety of ideas and perspectives that it brings forward. However, it’s crucial to draw a line and understand that every opinion does not warrant validation or even an audience. In fact, the relentless emphasis on sharing and placing value on everyone's opinion is causing more harm than good in many cases.

First and foremost, not every opinion is based on facts or well-informed research. With the current influx of misinformation on the internet, it is becoming increasingly difficult to separate fact from fiction. If each one of these misinformed opinions were to gain attention, it could lead to a widespread propagation of false information, causing potential harm.

Second, just because you hold an opinion strongly does not grant it the status of ‘universal truth’. An opinion, by definition, is a view or judgment formed about something, not necessarily based on fact or knowledge. People are entitled to their own beliefs and perspectives, but without proper evidence or compelling arguments to back this up, others under no obligation to accept or validate them.  

Lastly, not all opinions are created equal. Some are inherently harmful and hostile by promoting hatred, discrimination, or violence against certain groups of people. These opinions can be more than just disagreeable—they can be disrespectful, harmful or even dangerous.

That's not to say that we shouldn't have discussions, disagreements, and debates. We absolutely should because that's how we learn, grow and sometimes, even change our minds. But, let's not give every opinion an importance it may not deserve, let's not accept every standpoint as truth just because it's someone's opinion, and let's not feel obligated to validate an opinion just for the sake of being accommodating or polite. 

In sum, the freedom of speech that we value doesn't mean every opinion deserves credibility. With greater access to platforms to voice our thoughts, we must learn to differentiate between opinions that contribute positively to debates and discussions and those that don’t. Opinions are valuable, yes, but not all of them contribute to sensible, respectful, and constructive conversations.

prompt: Write a recipe for "Coconut Flan".
text:
Ingredients:

- 1 cup and 1/2 cup sugar
- 5 large eggs
- 1 can (14 ounces) sweetened condensed milk
- 1 can (13.5 ounces) unsweetened coconut milk
- 1 cup whole milk
- 1/2 cup unsweetened shredded coconut
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
- 1/2 teaspoon salt

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).

2. In a medium saucepan over medium heat, melt 1 cup sugar until it turns a golden-brown caramel. Be careful not to overcook it, or it will become bitter.

3. As soon as sugar has fully melted, pour into a 9-inch round cake pan, tilting the pan around to evenly distribute the caramel. Set aside.

4. In a blender, add the eggs, condensed milk, coconut milk, whole milk, the remaining 1/2 cup sugar, the shredded coconut, vanilla extract, and salt. Blend on high speed until the mixture is well combined.

5. Pour the custard mixture into the caramel-coated pan.

6. Place the cake pan in a large roasting pan and pour in enough hot water to come halfway up the sides of the cake pan.

7. Carefully place the baking dish in the preheated oven, and bake for about 50-60 minutes, or until the center is just set (it should still wobble slightly when pan is jiggled). 

8. Remove from oven and let it cool in the water bath until room temperature. Then refrigerate the flan for at least 4 hours or overnight.

9. To serve, run a knife around the edge of the cake pan to loosen the flan. Place a large serving platter over the cake pan, grasp both tightly together, and quickly invert them to allow the flan to drop onto the platter. Be sure to scrape out any remaining caramel from the pan onto the flan.

10. Garnish with extra shredded coconut before serving if desired.

Enjoy your delicious and creamy coconut flan!

systems are based upon a number of criteria. Probably the most important is the
number of mitotic figures which are most commonly determined as the mitotic
count (MC), i.e. number of mitotic figures within 10 consecutive high power
fields. Often the area with the highest mitotic activity is to be selected for

second step used to construct a mitotic activity estimate. Lastly, we select
the image segment representing the size of ten high power fields with the
overall highest mitotic activity as a region proposal for an expert MC
determination. We evaluate the approach using a dataset of 32 completely

To every human heart a mother-twin.

Knocking and knocking at the closed door;

If he stood knocking there for evermore.-
A mother angel, see! folding each wing,
Soft-walking, crosses straight the empty floor,
And opens to the obstinate praying thing.
8.
Were there but some deep, holy spell, whereby
Always I should remember thee-some mode
Of feeling the pure heat-throb momently
Of the spirit-fire still uttering this I!-
Lord, see thou to it, take thou remembrance' load:
Only when I bethink me can I cry;
Remember thou, and prick me with love's goad.

If to myself-'God sometimes interferes'-

I see him all in all, the lifing mind,

A love he is that watches and that hears,
Or but a mist fumed up from minds of men,
Whose fear and hope reach out beyond their ken.
10.
When I no more can stir my soul to move,
And life is but the ashes of a fire;
When I can but remember that my heart
Once used to live and love, long and aspire,-
Oh, be thou then the first, the one thou art;
Be thou the calling, before all answering love,
And in me wake hope, fear, boundless desire.

I thought that I had lost thee; but, behold!
Thou comest to me from the horizon low,
Across the fields outspread of green and gold-
Fair carpet for thy feet to come and go.
Whence I know not, or how to me thou art come!-
Not less my spirit with calm bliss doth glow,
Meeting thee only thus, in nature vague and dumb.
12.
Doubt swells and surges, with swelling doubt behind!
My soul in storm is but a tattered sail,
Streaming its ribbons on the torrent gale;
In calm, 'tis but a limp and flapping thing:
Oh! swell it with thy breath; make it a wing,-
To sweep through thee the ocean, with thee the wind
Nor rest until in thee its haven it shall find.
13.
The idle flapping of the sail is doubt;
Faith swells it full to breast the breasting seas.
Bold, conscience, fast, and rule the ruling helm;
Hell's freezing north no tempest can send out,
But it shall toss thee homeward to thy leas;
Boisterous wave-crest never shall o'erwhelm
Thy sea-float bark as safe as field-borne rooted elm.
14.
Sometimes, hard-trying, it seems I cannot pray-
For doubt, and pain, and anger, and all strife.
Yet some poor half-fledged prayer-bird from the nest
May fall, flit, fly, perch-crouch in the bowery breast
Of the large, nation-healing tree of life;-
Moveless there sit through all the burning day,
And on my heart at night a fresh leaf cooling lay.
15.
My harvest withers. Health, my means to live-
All things seem rushing straight into the dark.
But the dark still is God. I would not give
The smallest silver-piece to turn the rush
Backward or sideways. Am I not a spark
Of him who is the light?-Fair hope doth flush
My east.-Divine success-Oh, hush and hark!
16.
Thy will be done. I yield up everything.
'The life is more than meat'-then more than health;
'The body more than raiment'-then than wealth;
The hairs I made not, thou art numbering.
Thou art my life-I the brook, thou the spring.
Because thine eyes are open, I can see;
Because thou art thyself, 'tis therefore I am me.
17.
No sickness can come near to blast my health;
My life depends not upon any meat;
My bread comes not from any human tilth;
No wings will grow upon my changeless wealth;
Wrong cannot touch it, violence or deceit;
Thou art my life, my health, my bank, my barn-
And from all other gods thou plain dost warn.
18.
Care thou for mine whom I must leave behind;
Care that they know who 'tis for them takes care;
Thy present patience help them still to bear;
Lord, keep them clearing, growing, heart and mind;
In one thy oneness us together bind;
Last earthly prayer with which to thee I cling-
Grant that, save love, we owe not anything.
19.
'Tis well, for unembodied thought a live,
True house to build-of stubble, wood, nor hay;
So, like bees round the flower by which they thrive,
My thoughts are busy with the informing truth,
And as I build, I feed, and grow in youth-
Hoping to stand fresh, clean, and strong, and gay,
When up the east comes dawning His great day.
20.
Thy will is truth-'tis therefore fate, the strong.
Would that my will did sweep full swing with thine!
Then harmony with every spheric song,
And conscious power, would give sureness divine.
Who thinks to thread thy great laws' onward throng,
Is as a fly that creeps his foolish way
Athwart an engine's wheels in smooth resistless play.
21.
Thou in my heart hast planted, gardener divine,
A scion of the tree of life: it grows;
But not in every wind or weather it blows;
The leaves fall sometimes from the baby tree,
And the life-power seems melting into pine;
Yet still the sap keeps struggling to the shine,
And the unseen root clings cramplike unto thee.
22.
Do thou, my God, my spirit's weather control;
And as I do not gloom though the day be dun,
Let me not gloom when earth-born vapours roll
Across the infinite zenith of my soul.
Should sudden brain-frost through the heart's summer run,
Cold, weary, joyless, waste of air and sun,
Thou art my south, my summer-wind, my all, my one.
23.
O Life, why dost thou close me up in death?
O Health, why make me inhabit heaviness?-
I ask, yet know: the sum of this distress,
Pang-haunted body, sore-dismayed mind,
Is but the egg that rounds the winged faith;
When that its path into the air shall find,
My heart will follow, high above cold, rain, and wind.
24.
I can no more than lift my weary eyes;
Therefore I lift my weary eyes-no more.
But my eyes pull my heart, and that, before
'Tis well awake, knocks where the conscience lies;
Conscience runs quick to the spirit's hidden door:
Straightway, from every sky-ward window, cries
Up to the Father's listening ears arise.
25.
Not in my fancy now I search to find thee;
Not in its loftiest forms would shape or bind thee;
I cry to one whom I can never know,
Filling me with an infinite overflow;
Not to a shape that dwells within my heart,
Clothed in perfections love and truth assigned thee,
But to the God thou knowest that thou art.
26.
Not, Lord, because I have done well or ill;
Not that my mind looks up to thee clear-eyed;
Not that it struggles in fast cerements tied;
Not that I need thee daily sorer still;
Not that I wretched, wander from thy will;
Not now for any cause to thee I cry,
But this, that thou art thou, and here am I.
27.
Yestereve, Death came, and knocked at my thin door.
I from my window looked: the thing I saw,
The shape uncouth, I had not seen before.
I was disturbed-with fear, in sooth, not awe;
Whereof ashamed, I instantly did rouse
My will to seek thee-only to fear the more:
Alas! I could not find thee in the house.
28.
I was like Peter when he began to sink.
To thee a new prayer therefore I have got-
That, when Death comes in earnest to my door,
Thou wouldst thyself go, when the latch doth clink,
And lead him to my room, up to my cot;
Then hold thy child's hand, hold and leave him not,
Till Death has done with him for evermore.
29.
Till Death has done with him?-Ah, leave me then!
And Death has done with me, oh, nevermore!
He comes-and goes-to leave me in thy arms,
Nearer thy heart, oh, nearer than before!
To lay thy child, naked, new-born again
Of mother earth, crept free through many harms,
Upon thy bosom-still to the very core.
30.
Come to me, Lord: I will not speculate how,
Nor think at which door I would have thee appear,
Nor put off calling till my floors be swept,
But cry, 'Come, Lord, come any way, come now.'
Doors, windows, I throw wide; my head I bow,
And sit like some one who so long has slept
That he knows nothing till his life draw near.
31.
O Lord, I have been talking to the people;
Thought's wheels have round me whirled a fiery zone,
And the recoil of my words' airy ripple
My heart unheedful has puffed up and blown.
Therefore I cast myself before thee prone:
Lay cool hands on my burning brain, and press
From my weak heart the swelling emptiness.

prompt: Write a recipe for "Frozen Peanut Butter and Banana Bars".
text:
Ingredients:
1 cup rolled oats
1/2 cup peanut butter
1/2 cup honey
1 tsp vanilla extract
1/4 tsp salt
2 ripe bananas, mashed
1 cup frozen mixed berries (strawberries, blueberries, raspberries, etc.)
1/2 cup chocolate chips

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit.
2. In a medium-sized bowl, mix together the rolled oats, peanut butter, honey, vanilla extract, and salt until well incorporated.
3. Stir in the mashed bananas until the mixture is evenly distributed.
4. Fold in the frozen mixed berries and chocolate chips.
5. Line a 9x9 inch baking dish with parchment paper.
6. Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish and press down evenly.
7. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the edges are golden brown.
8. Allow to cool completely before slicing into bars and freezing for at least 2 hours, or until firm. Enjoy!

prompt: Write a recipe for "Provencal Bean Pot".
text:
Recipe: Provencal Bean Pot

Ingredients:
- 2 cups white beans, soaked overnight and drained
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 large onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1 yellow bell pepper, diced
- 2 zucchinis, diced
- 1 eggplant, diced
- 4 tomatoes, diced
- 2 tablespoons tomato paste
- 1 teaspoon dried thyme
- 1 teaspoon dried oregano
- 1 bay leaf
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped for garnish

Instructions:

1. In a large pot, heat the olive oil over medium-high heat. Add the diced onion and minced garlic and sauté until fragrant and translucent, about 5 minutes.

2. Add the diced bell peppers, zucchinis, and eggplant to the pot and cook for another 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.

3. Stir in the diced tomatoes and tomato paste. Cook for another 2 minutes.

4. Add the soaked and drained white beans to the pot and enough water to cover the beans by about an inch. Add the dried thyme, oregano, and bay leaf. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

5. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and cover the pot. Simmer for about 1 ½ to 2 hours, or until the beans are tender and the flavors have melded together.

6. Remove the bay leaf from the pot and taste for seasoning. Adjust the salt and pepper if needed.

7. Serve the Provencal bean pot hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley. This dish pairs well with a crusty bread or can be served over rice or quinoa.

Enjoy your delicious Provencal Bean Pot!

- 1 block of firm tofu

On 16 March 1912, Oates famously walked out into a blizzard, stating "I am just going outside, and may be some time", to sacrifice himself and give the remaining team members a better chance of survival. His body was never recovered.

== Legacy and honours ==
Oates's courage and selflessness became legendary and he continues to be honoured in Britain and beyond. Memorials to Oates stand at the Church of St. George in Meanwood, Leeds, and the Scott Polar Research Institute in Cambridge. 

In 1985, the Lawrence Oates School was opened in Farnborough, Hampshire, and in 2012, a Royal Mail stamp was issued commemorating the centenary of Oates's selfless act.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have shown to be powerful medical image
segmentation models. In this study, we address some of the main unresolved
issues regarding these models. Specifically, training of these models on small
medical image datasets is still challenging, with many studies promoting
techniques such as transfer learning. Moreover, these models are infamous for
producing over-confident predictions and for failing silently when presented
with out-of-distribution (OOD) data at test time. In this paper, we advocate
for multi-task learning, i.e., training a single model on several different
datasets, spanning several different organs of interest and different imaging
modalities. We show that not only a single CNN learns to automatically
recognize the context and accurately segment the organ of interest in each
context, but also that such a joint model often has more accurate and
better-calibrated predictions than dedicated models trained separately on each
dataset. Our experiments show that multi-task learning can outperform transfer
learning in medical image segmentation tasks. For detecting OOD data, we
propose a method based on spectral analysis of CNN feature maps. We show that
different datasets, representing different imaging modalities and/or different
organs of interest, have distinct spectral signatures, which can be used to
identify whether or not a test image is similar to the images used to train a
model. We show that this approach is far more accurate than OOD detection based
on prediction uncertainty. The methods proposed in this paper contribute
significantly to improving the accuracy and reliability of CNN-based medical
image segmentation models.

Ingredients for Duck Dumplings:

For the Filling:
- 1 whole duck
- 1 tablespoon soy sauce
- 1 teaspoon Chinese five-spice powder
- 1 teaspoon sugar 
- 1/4 cup hoisin sauce
- 2 green onions, finely chopped
- 1/2 cup diced water chestnuts
- 1 garlic clove, minced
- 1 tablespoon grated fresh ginger

For the Dumplings:
- 40 dumpling wrappers
- Small bowl of water, for assembling dumplings
- canola oil, for frying

For the Dipping sauce:
- 1/2 cup soy sauce
- 1/4 cup rice vinegar
- 2 teaspoons sesame oil
- 1 teaspoon sugar 
- 1 green onion, chopped

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C). Place the duck on a rack in a roasting pan and season with soy sauce, sugar, and Chinese five-spice. Roast the duck in the oven for about 2 hours or until the internal temperature reaches 165°F  (75°C).

2. While the duck is roasting, prepare the dipping sauce by whisking together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sugar and chopped green onion in a small bowl. Set aside.

3. When the duck is done, remove it from oven and set aside until cool enough to handle. Shred the duck meat, discarding the skin and bones.

4. In a large bowl, combine shredded duck meat, hoisin sauce, chopped green onions, diced water chestnuts, minced garlic and grated ginger. Stir until well combined.

5. Lay out the dumpling wrappers out on a clean work surface. Scoop about 1 tablespoon of the duck mixture onto the center of each wrapper.

6. Dip your finger in the bowl of water and run it around the edge of each dumpling wrapper. Fold the wrapper over the filling to create a semi-circle, and press the edges together to seal.

7. Heat a large pan over medium heat and add a little bit of oil. Add the dumplings in batches, ensuring they don’t touch each other, and pan-fry until the bottoms are golden brown, about 3-4 minutes.

text:
Ingredients:
- 4 1/2 cups of prepared fruit (about 3 pounds fully ripe apricots and 2 cans (20 oz. each) crushed pineapple in 100% juice, undrained)
- 1 cup crushed pineapple with juice
- 2 boxes MCP Pectin
- 1/2 teaspoon butter or margarine
- 7 cups granulated sugar

Instructions:
1. Pit ripe apricots (do not peel), cut into pieces and finely chop, or grind.
2. Measure exact amount of prepared fruit into 6 or 8-qt.sauce pot. Stir pineapple with juice into fruit in sauce pot. Stir fruit pectin into fruit in sauce pot. Add butter to reduce foaming.
3. Bring mixture to a full rolling boil (a boil that doesn't stop bubbling when stirred) on high heat, stirring constantly.  
4. Stir in exact amount of sugar quickly. Return to a full rolling boil and boil exactly 4 minutes, stirring constantly. Remove from heat. Skim off any foam with a metal spoon.
5. Ladle quickly into prepared jars, filling within 1/8" of tops. Wipe jar rims and threads with a clean damp cloth. Cover with two-piece lids. Screw bands tightly. 
6. Process in a boiling water bath for about 10 minutes, adjusting for altitude, if necessary. Make sure the jars are fully submerged and covered with at least 1 inch of water.
7. Let jars stand on a towel to cool for 24 hours; check seals. Any unsealed jars should be refrigerated and used within a few weeks.
8. Store jam in cool, dark place up to 1 year.

Notes:

- Yield: about 8 - (1 cup) jars
- Be sure to not peel the apricots. Peeling them will affect the texture of the jam.

text:
Ingredients:

- 3/4 cup warm water (110°-115° F)
- 1/4 cup sugar
- 1 packet (2 1/4 tsp) active dry yeast
- 1 egg, slightly beaten
- 1/2 cup evaporated milk
- 3 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 2 tbsp soft unsalted butter
- Vegetable oil for frying (enough to fill the pan 2-3 inches deep)
- Powdered sugar for dusting

Instructions:

1. In a large bowl, combine the warm water and sugar. Stir until the sugar is fully dissolved.
2. Sprinkle the yeast over the sugar water. Let it sit for about 5 minutes, or until it becomes foamy.
3. Add the beaten egg and evaporated milk to the yeast mixture. Stir until combined.
4. In another bowl, mix together the flour and salt. Gradually add this to the yeast mixture, stirring continuously until a soft, sticky dough forms.
5. Add the butter to the dough, continue to mix until the butter is fully incorporated.
6. Transfer the dough to a lightly floured surface. Knead for 2-3 minutes or until smooth and no longer sticky. Add more flour if necessary.
7. Place the dough in a greased bowl and cover with a damp cloth. Let it rise in a warm place for 2 hours, or until it doubles in size.
8. Once the dough has risen, punch it down and turn it out onto a floured surface. Roll the dough out to about 1/4-inch thick.
9. Cut the dough into squares or rectangles, typically about 2.5 inches on each side.
10. In a deep fryer or large pan, heat the vegetable oil to 375° F.
11. Carefully drop the dough squares, a few at a time, into the hot oil. Fry for 1-2 minutes on each side, or until golden brown.
12. Use a slotted spoon to remove the beignets from the oil. Drain them on a kitchen towel or paper towel.
13. Sprinkle a generous amount of powdered sugar over the hot beignets.
14. Serve warm and enjoy your homemade beignets! 

Note: Beignets are best served fresh, so try to consume them shortly after frying. They also pair well with a cup of strong coffee.

prompt: Write a recipe for "Avocado Cake With Avocado Buttercream".
text:
Ingredients:

For the Cake:

- 3 ripe avocados, pitted and peeled
- 2 cups granulated sugar
- 3 eggs
- 1 cup vegetable oil
- 2 teaspoons vanilla extract
- 3 cups all-purpose flour
- 2 teaspoons baking powder
- 1 teaspoon baking soda
- 1/2 teaspoon salt

For the Avocado Buttercream:

- 2 ripe avocados, peeled and pitted 
- 1 cup unsalted butter, at room temperature 
- 5 cups powdered sugar 
- 1 teaspoon lemon juice
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and flour two 9-inch round cake pans and set aside.

2. In a large bowl, mash the avocados until smooth. Add the granulated sugar, eggs, vegetable oil, and vanilla extract, mixing until well combined.

3. In a separate bowl, combine the all-purpose flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the avocado mixture, stirring until just combined.

4. Divide the batter evenly between the prepared cake pans and smooth the tops with a spatula. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center of the cakes comes out clean. Allow the cakes to cool in the pans for 10 minutes, then transfer them to wire racks to cool completely.

5. While the cakes are cooling, prepare the avocado buttercream. In a large bowl, beat the avocados and butter until smooth. Gradually add the powdered sugar, beating until light and fluffy. Stir in the lemon juice and vanilla extract.

6. Once the cakes have cooled, spread a layer of the avocado buttercream on one cake layer. Place the second cake layer on top, then spread the remaining buttercream over the top and sides of the cake.

7. Serve and enjoy your avocado cake with avocado buttercream.

Note:

The avocados should be well ripe for smoother texture and better taste. If you want less sweet buttercream, you can reduce the amount of powdered sugar.

prompt: Write the abstract for the academic paper titled "ACCL: Adversarial constrained-CNN loss for weakly supervised medical image segmentation".
text:
In this paper, we propose a novel loss function called Adversarial Constrained-CNN Loss (ACCL) for weakly supervised medical image segmentation. The goal of weakly supervised segmentation is to train deep learning models to accurately segment medical images using only weak labels, such as image-level class labels or scribbles, instead of precise segmentation masks. However, existing weakly supervised segmentation methods suffer from two major limitations: 1) lack of spatial information, as the models are not guided by precise segmentation masks, and 2) reliance on large annotated datasets, which are time-consuming and expensive to obtain.

To address these limitations, we introduce ACCL, which incorporates adversarial and constrained regularizations to improve the accuracy of weakly supervised segmentation. The adversarial regularization encourages the model to produce segmentation masks that are similar to those generated by a fully supervised model, while the constrained regularization ensures that the model respects the image-level class labels and spatial constraints. We evaluate ACCL on several publicly available medical datasets and show that it outperforms existing weakly supervised segmentation methods. Our experiments also demonstrate that ACCL is robust to different types of weak labels and can adapt to various medical image segmentation tasks.

ACCL has the potential to significantly reduce the annotation effort required for medical image segmentation, making it possible to train models with high accuracy using only weak labels. This work paves the way for using deep learning models in medical image analysis tasks where annotated data is scarce or difficult to obtain.

1. ON A RHINE STEAMER.
Republic of the West,
Enlightened, free, sublime,
Unquestionably best
Production of our time.
The telephone is thine,
And thine the Pullman Car,
The caucus, the divine
Intense electric star.
To thee we likewise owe
The venerable names
Of Edgar Allan Poe,
And Mr. Henry James.
In short it's due to thee,
Thou kind of Western star,
That we have come to be
Precisely what we are.
But every now and then,
It cannot be denied,
You breed a kind of men
Who are not dignified,
Or courteous or refined,
Benevolent or wise,
Or gifted with a mind
Beyond the common size,
Or notable for tact,
Agreeable to me,
Or anything, in fact,
That people ought to be.

Britannia rules the waves,
As I have heard her say;
She frees whatever slaves
She meets upon her way.
A teeming mother she
Of Parliaments and Laws;
Majestic, mighty, free:
Devoid of common flaws.
For here did Shakspere write
His admirable plays:
For her did Nelson fight
And Wolseley win his bays.
Her sturdy common sense
Is based on solid grounds:
By saving numerous pence
She spends effective pounds.
The Saxon and the Celt
She equitably rules;
Her iron rod is felt
By countless knaves and fools.
In fact, mankind at large,
Black, yellow, white and red,
Is given to her in charge,
And owns her as a head.

Unworthy of a man:
A look of dull surprise;
A nerveless idle hand:
An eye which never tries
To threaten or command:
In short, a kind of man,
If man indeed he be,
As worthy of our ban
As any that we see:
Unspeakably obtuse,
Abominably vain,
Of very little use,
And execrably plain.

- 1/4 teaspoon paprika
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 1/4 cup vegetable oil or melted butter for frying

CE-Net: Context Encoder Network for 2D Medical Image Segmentation
Abstract:

We propose a context encoder network (CE-Net), which learns the spatial dependencies in the context of medical images, and exploits this information to improve the performance of the segmentation task. We evaluate the CE-Net on two publicly available datasets: the MIMO-CAD dataset and the OASIS dataset. Our results show that the CE-Net outperforms the state-of-the-art models on both datasets. The CE-Net is also trained faster than the existing models, which makes it a more practical solution for medical image segmentation.

The revival began earlier with historical discoveries and early modern publications dealing with Old Norse culture. The first printed edition of the 13th century Gesta Danorum or the Legend of the Danes by Saxo Grammaticus, came out in 1514 just as book printing began become more practical and printing trade was quickly spreading. In 1555, the Historia de gentibus septentrionalibus, or "History of the northern peoples", by Olaus Magnus was produced. The pace of publication increased during the 17th century with Latin translations of the famous Edda, notably Peder Resen's Edda Islandorum of 1665. The Edda consisted of two 13th century Medieval Icelandic literary works on Norse mythology, written down in the 13th century, but certainly from older oral sources: they are the Prose Edda, and an older collection of poems without an original title now known as the Poetic Edda. (The term historically referred only to the Prose Edda, but this since has fallen out of use because of the confusion with the other work.) The books are the main sources of medieval skaldic tradition of poetry and storytelling in Iceland and Norse mythology. The word Viking is not a medieval term; it was only introduced into Modern English during the 18th century. At that point in the Romantic Era, Viking exploits were aggregated, and tended to be falsely subsumed under a single category and subsequently romanticized as heroic adventure. Etymologists frequently trace the word "Viking" to writers who are referring to those who set about to raid and pillage. The word Viking in the sense in which it is commonly used is derived from the Old Norse víkingr signifying a sea-rover or pirate.
