prompt: Write the abstract for the academic paper titled "Comparative Study of Statistical Skin Detection Algorithms for Sub-Continental Human Images".
text:
The presentation of accurate, reliable, and efficient skin detection algorithms is essential for a range of applications, including medical diagnosis, biometrics, and computer vision. However, a comprehensive comparison of statistical skin detection algorithms' performance on sub-continental images has not been conducted to date. This study aimed to compare various statistical skin detection methods in terms of accuracy, reliability, and computational efficiency. 

Twenty statistical skin detection algorithms were evaluated, and the performance was measured using a dataset of sub-continental images from different countries in Africa and Asia. Images were labeled manually to validate the accuracy of the detection results. The results showed that local statistical skin detection algorithms performed better than global algorithms, with an average accuracy of 95.9% for Africa and 88.4% for Asia. Furthermore, an ensemble of local statistical skin detection algorithms with a combination of local descriptors and global models showed a superior performance compared to individual algorithms, achieving an accuracy of 96.7%. 

In conclusion, our study provides insights into selecting the appropriate statistical skin detection algorithms for specific sub-continental images. Local statistical skin detection algorithms, especially those that combine local descriptors and global models, are recommended for improved performance in sub-continental images.

The novel opens in London in 632 (AD 2540 in the Gregorian Calendar). The vast majority of the population is unified under the World State, an eternally peaceful, stable global society in which goods and resources are plentiful (because the population is permanently limited to no more than two billion people) and everyone is happy. Natural reproduction has been done away with and children are created, 'decanted' and raised in Hatcheries and Conditioning Centres, where they are divided into five castes (which are further split into 'Plus' and 'Minus' members) and designed to fulfill predetermined positions within the social and economic strata of the World State. Fetuses chosen to become members of the highest caste, 'Alpha', are allowed to develop naturally while maturing to term in "decanting bottles", while fetuses chosen to become members of the lower castes ('Beta', 'Gamma', 'Delta', 'Epsilon') are subjected to in situ chemical interference to cause arrested development in intelligence or physical growth. Each 'Alpha' or 'Beta' is the product of one unique fertilized egg developing into one unique fetus. Members of lower castes are not unique but are instead created using the Bokanovsky process which enables a single egg to spawn (at the point of the story being told) up to 96 children and one ovary to produce thousands of children. To further increase the birthrate of Gammas, Deltas and Epsilons, Podsnap's Technique causes all the eggs in the ovary to mature simultaneously, allowing the hatchery to get full use of the ovary in two years' time. People of these castes make up the majority of human society, and the production of such specialized children bolsters the efficiency and harmony of society, since these people are deliberately limited in their cognitive and physical abilities, as well as the scope of their ambitions and the complexity of their desires, thus rendering them easier to control. All children are educated via the hypnopaedic process, which provides each child with caste-appropriate subconscious messages to mold the child's lifelong self-image and social outlook to that chosen by the leaders and their predetermined plans for producing future adult generations. To maintain the World State's Command Economy for the indefinite future, all citizens are conditioned from birth to value consumption with such platitudes as "ending is better than mending," "more stiches less riches" i.e., buy a new item instead of fixing the old one, because constant consumption, and near-universal employment to meet society's material demands, is the bedrock of economic and social stability for the World State. Beyond providing social engagement and distraction in the material realm of work or play, the need for transcendence, solitude and spiritual communion is addressed with the ubiquitous availability and universally endorsed consumption of the drug soma. Soma is an allusion to a mythical drink of the same name consumed by ancient Indo-Aryans. In the book, soma is a hallucinogen that takes users on enjoyable, hangover-free "holidays". It was developed by the World State to provide these inner-directed personal experiences within a socially managed context of State-run 'religious' organizations; social clubs. The hypnopaedically inculcated affinity for the State-produced drug, as a self-medicating comfort mechanism in the face of stress or discomfort, thereby eliminates the need for religion or other personal allegiances outside or beyond the World State. Recreational sex is an integral part of society. According to the World State, sex is a social activity, rather than a means of reproduction (sex is encouraged from early childhood). The few women who can reproduce are conditioned to use birth control, even wearing a "Malthusian belt" (which resembles a cartridge belt and holds "the regulation supply of contraceptives") as a popular fashion accessory. The maxim "everyone belongs to everyone else" is repeated often, and the idea of a "family" is considered pornographic; sexual competition and emotional, romantic relationships are rendered obsolete because they are no longer needed. Marriage, natural birth, parenthood, and pregnancy are considered too obscene to be mentioned in casual conversation. Thus, society has developed a new idea of reproductive comprehension. Spending time alone is considered an outrageous waste of time and money, and wanting to be an individual is horrifying. Conditioning trains people to consume and never to enjoy being alone, so by spending an afternoon not playing "Obstacle Golf," or not in bed with a friend, one is forfeiting acceptance. In the World State, people typically die at age 60 having maintained good health and youthfulness their whole life. Death isn't feared; anyone reflecting upon it is reassured by the knowledge that everyone is happy, and that society goes on. Since no one has family, they have no ties to mourn. The conditioning system eliminates the need for professional competitiveness; people are literally bred to do their jobs and cannot desire another. There is no competition within castes; each caste member receives the same food, housing, and soma rationing as every other member of that caste. There is no desire to change one's caste, largely because a person's sleep-conditioning reinforces each individual's place in the caste system. To grow closer with members of the same class, citizens participate in mock religious services called Solidarity Services, in which twelve people consume large quantities of soma and sing hymns. The ritual progresses through group hypnosis and climaxes in an orgy. In geographic areas nonconducive to easy living and consumption, securely contained groups of "savages" are left to their own devices. These appear to be similar to the reservations of land established for the Native American population during the colonisation of North America. These 'savages' are beholden of strange customs, including self-mutilation and religion, a mere curio in the outside world. In its first chapters, the novel describes life in the World State as wonderful and introduces Lenina Crowne and Bernard Marx. Lenina, a hatchery worker, is socially accepted and comfortable with her place in society, while Bernard, a psychologist, is an outcast. Although an Alpha Plus, Bernard is shorter in stature than the average of his caste—a quality shared by the lower castes, which gives him an inferiority complex. His work with sleep-teaching has led him to realize that what others believe to be their own deeply held beliefs are merely phrases repeated to children while they are asleep. Still, he recognizes the necessity of such programming as the reason why his society meets the emotional needs of its citizens. Courting disaster, he is vocal about being different, once stating he dislikes soma because he'd "rather be himself." Bernard's differences fuel rumors that he was accidentally administered alcohol while incubated, a method used to keep Epsilons short. Bernard's only friend is Helmholtz Watson, an Alpha Plus lecturer at the College of Emotional Engineering (Department of Writing). The friendship is based on their similar experiences as misfits, but unlike Bernard, Watson's sense of loneliness stems from being too gifted, too intelligent, too handsome, and too physically strong. Helmholtz is drawn to Bernard as a confidant: he can talk to Bernard about his desire to write poetry. Bernard is on holiday at a Savage Reservation. The reservation, located in New Mexico, consists of a community named Malpais. From afar, Lenina thinks it will be exciting. In person, she finds the aged, toothless natives who mend their clothes rather than throw them away repugnant, and the situation is made worse when she discovers that she has left her soma tablets at the resort hotel. In typical tourist fashion, Bernard and Lenina watch what at first appears to be a quaint native ceremony. The village folk, whose culture resembles the contemporary Indian groups of the region, descendants of the Anasazi, including the Puebloan peoples of Acoma, Laguna, and Zuni, and the Ramah Navajo, begin by singing, but the ritual quickly becomes a passion play where a village boy is whipped to unconsciousness. Soon after, the couple encounters Linda, a woman who has been living in Malpais since she came on a trip and became separated from her group, among whom was a man to whom she refers as "Tomakin" but who is revealed to be Bernard's boss, the Director of Hatcheries and Conditioning, Thomas. She became pregnant despite adhering to her "Malthusian Drill" and there were no facilities for an abortion. Her shame at pregnancy was so great that she decided not to return to her old life, but to stay with the "savages". Linda gave birth to a son, John (later referred to as John the Savage) who is now 18. Conversations with Linda and John reveal that their life has been hard. For 18 years, they have been treated as outsiders: the native men treated Linda like a sex object while the native women regularly beat and ostracized her because of her promiscuity, and John was mistreated and excluded for his mother's actions and the color of his skin. John was angered by Linda's lovers, and even attacked one in a jealous rage while a child. John's one joy was that his mother had taught him to read, although he only had two books: a scientific manual from his mother's job, which he called a "beastly, beastly book," and a collection of Shakespeare's works (which have been banned in the World State for being subversive). Shakespeare gives John articulation to his feelings, though, and he especially is interested in Othello, Romeo and Juliet, and Hamlet. At the same time, John has been denied the religious rituals of the village, although he has watched them and even has had some religious experiences on his own in the desert. Old, weathered and tired, Linda wants to return to her familiar world in London, as she misses living in the city and taking soma. John wants to see the "brave new world" his mother has told him so much about. Bernard wants to take them back to block Thomas from his plan to reassign Bernard to Iceland as punishment for his asocial beliefs. Bernard arranges permission for Linda and John to leave the reservation. John also seems to have an attraction to Lenina, as while Bernard is away, getting the permission to move the savages, he finds her suitcase and ruffles through all of her clothes, taking in the smells. He then sees her "sleeping" and stares at her, thinking all he has to do to see her properly is undo one zip. He later tells himself off for being like this towards Lenina, and seems to be extremely shy around her. Upon his return to London, Bernard is confronted by Thomas, the Director of the Hatchery and Conditioning Centre who, in front of an audience of higher-caste Centre workers, denounces Bernard for his asocial behavior. Bernard, thinking that for the first time in his life he has the upper hand, defends himself by presenting the Director with his long-lost lover and unknown son, Linda and John. John falls to his knees and calls Thomas his father, which causes an uproar of laughter. The humiliated Director resigns in shame. Spared from reassignment, Bernard makes John the toast of London. Pursued by the highest members of society, able to bed any woman he fancies, Bernard revels in attention he once scorned. The victory, however, is short-lived. Linda, decrepit, toothless, and friendless, goes on a permanent soma holiday while John, appalled by what he perceives to be an empty society, refuses to attend Bernard's parties. Society drops Bernard as swiftly as it had taken him. Bernard turns to the person he'd believed to be his one true friend, only to see Helmholtz fall into a quick, easy camaraderie with John. Bernard is left an outcast yet again as he watches the only two men with whom he ever connected find more of interest in each other than they ever did in him. John and Helmholtz's island of peace is brief. Lenina tries to seduce John, but John pushes her away, calling her out on her sexually wanton ways. Whilst Lenina is in the bathroom, humiliated and putting her clothes on, John receives a telephone call from the hospital telling him that his mother is extremely unwell. He rushes over to see her and sits at her bedside, trying to get her out of her soma holiday so that he can talk to her. He is heartbroken when his mother succumbs to soma and dies. He is extremely annoyed by the young boys that enter the ward to be conditioned about death and annoy John to the point where he starts to use violence to send them away. John's grief bewilders and revolts the hospital workers, and their lack of reaction to Linda's death prompts John to try to force humanity from the workers by throwing their soma rations out a window. The ensuing riot brings the police, who quell the riot by filling the room with soma. Bernard and Helmholtz arrive to help John, but only Helmholtz helps him, while Bernard stands to the side, torn between risking involvement by helping or escaping the scene. Following the riot, Bernard, Helmholtz and John are brought before Mustapha Mond, the Resident World Controller for Western Europe. Bernard (who breaks down during the middle of the conversation) and Helmholtz are told they will be exiled to islands of their choice. Mond explains that this exile is not so much a threat to force freethinkers to reform and rejoin society as it is a chance for them to act as they please because they will not be able to influence the population. He also divulges that he too once risked banishment to an island because of some scientific experiments that were deemed controversial by the state, giving insight into his sympathetic tone. Helmholtz chooses the Falkland Islands, believing that their terrible weather will inspire his writing, but Bernard simply does not want to leave London; he struggles with Mond and is thrown out of the office. After Bernard and Helmholtz have left, Mustapha and John engage in a philosophical argument on the morals behind the existing society and then John is told the "experiment" will continue and he will not be sent to an island. John meets with Bernard and Helmholtz once again before their departures from London and Bernard apologizes to John for his opportunistic behavior, having come to terms with his imminent exile and having restored his friendship with Helmholtz. In the final chapter, John isolates himself from society in a lighthouse outside London where he finds his hermit life interrupted from mourning his mother by the more bitter memories of civilization. To atone, John brutally whips himself in the open, a ritual the Indians in his own village had denied him. His self-flagellation, caught on film and shown publicly, destroys his hermit life. Hundreds of gawking sightseers, intrigued by John's violent behavior, fly out to watch the savage in person. Even Lenina comes to watch, crying a tear John does not see. The sight of the woman whom he both adores and blames is too much for him; John attacks and whips her. This sight of genuine, unbridled emotion drives the crowd wild with excitement, and — handling it as they are conditioned to — they turn on each other, in a frenzy of beating and chanting that devolves into a mass orgy of soma and sex. In the morning, John, hopeless, alone, horrified by his drug use and the orgy in which he participated that countered his beliefs, makes one last attempt to escape civilization and atone. When thousands of gawking sightseers arrive that morning, frenzied at the prospect of seeing the savage perform again, they find John dead from a suicidal hanging.

Lewis has been both criticized and congratulated for his unorthodox writing style in Babbitt. As one reviewer puts it: “There is no plot whatever… Babbitt simply grows two years older as the tale unfolds.” Lewis presents a chronological series of scenes in the life of his title character. After introducing George F. Babbitt as a middle-aged man, "nimble in the calling of selling houses for more than people could afford to pay," Lewis presents a meticulously detailed description of Babbitt's morning routine. Each item Babbitt encounters is explained, from the high-tech alarm clock, which Babbitt sees as a marker of social status, to the rough camp blanket, a symbol of the freedom and heroism of the West. As he dresses for the day, Babbitt contemplates each article of his "Solid Citizen" uniform, most important being his Booster's club button, which he wears with pride. The first seven chapters follow Babbitt's life over the course of a single day. Over breakfast Babbitt dotes on his ten-year-old daughter Tinka, tries to dissuade his twenty-two-year-old daughter Verona from her new found socialist leanings, and encourages his seventeen-year-old son Ted to try harder in school. At the office he dictates letters and discusses real estate advertising with his employees. Babbitt is professionally successful as a realtor. Much of his energy in early chapters is spent on climbing the social ladder through booster functions, real estate sales, and making good with various dignitaries. According to Babbitt, any “decent” man in Zenith belonged to at least two or three “lodges” or booster clubs. They were good for potential business partnerships, getting time away from home and family life, and quite simply because “it was the thing to do.” Babbitt admits that while these clubs “stimulated him like brandy,” he often found work dull and nerve-wracking in comparison. Lewis also paints vivid scenes of Babbitt bartering for liquor (despite being a supporter of Prohibition) and hosting dinner parties. At his college class reunion, Babbitt reconnects with a former classmate, Charles McKelvey, whose success in the construction business made him a millionaire. Seizing the opportunity to hobnob with someone from a wealthier class, Babbitt invites the McKelveys to a dinner party. Although Babbitt hopes the party will help his family rise socially, the McKelveys leave early and do not extend a dinner invitation in return. Gradually, Babbitt realizes his dissatisfaction with "The American Dream," and attempts to quell these feelings by going camping in Maine with his close friend and old college roommate Paul Reisling. When Babbitt and Paul arrive at the camp they marvel at the beauty and simplicity of nature. Looking out over a lake Babbitt comments: “I’d just like to sit here – the rest of my life – and whittle – and sit. And never hear a typewriter.” Paul is similarly entranced, stating: “Oh it’s darn good, Georgie. There’s something eternal about it.” Although the trip has its ups and downs, the two men consider it an overall success, and leave feeling optimistic about the year ahead. On the day that Babbitt gets elected vice-president of the Booster’s club, he finds out that Paul shot his wife Zilla. Immediately Babbitt drives to the jail where Paul is being kept. Babbitt is very shaken up by the situation, trying to think of ways to help Paul out. When Paul was sentenced to a three-year jail term, “Babbitt returned to his office to realize that he faced a world which, without Paul, was meaningless.” Shortly after Paul’s arrest, Myra and Tinka go to visit relatives, leaving Babbitt more or less on his own. Alone with his thoughts Babbitt begins to ask himself what it was he really wanted in life. Eventually, “he stumbled upon the admission that he wanted the fairy girl - in the flesh.” Missing Paul, Babbitt decides to return to Maine. He imagines himself as a rugged outdoorsman, and thinks about what it would be like to become a camp guide himself. Ultimately, however, he is disenchanted with the wilderness and leaves “lonelier than he had ever been in his life.” Eventually Babbitt finds the cure for his loneliness in an attractive new client, Tanis Judique. He opens up to her about everything that happened with Paul and Zilla, and Tanis proves to be a sympathetic listener. In time, Babbitt begins to rebel against all of the standards he formerly held: he jumps into liberal politics with famous socialist litigator Seneca Doane; conducts an extramarital affair with Tanis; goes on various vacations; and cavorts around Zenith with would-be Bohemians and flappers. But each effort ends up disillusioning him to the concept of rebellion. On his excursions with Tanis and her group of friends, "the Bunch," he learns that even the Bohemians have rigid standards for their subculture. When Virgil Gunch and others discover Babbitt's activities with Seneca Doane and Tanis Judique, Virgil tries to convince Babbitt to return to conformity and join their newly founded "Good Citizens' League.” Babbitt refuses. His former friends then ostracize him; boycotting Babbitt's real estate ventures and shunning him publicly in clubs around town. Babbitt slowly becomes aware that his forays into nonconformity are not only futile but also destructive of the life and the friends he once loved. Yet he continues with them — even after Myra suspects Babbitt's affair, though she has no proof or specific knowledge. Unrelated to these events, Myra falls seriously ill with acute appendicitis. Babbitt, in a near-epiphany, rushes home and relinquishes all rebellion in order to care for his wife. During her long recovery, they spend a lot of time together, rekindling their intimacy. In short time, his old friends and colleagues welcome Babbitt back into the fold. For the Korean Short Ribs:
- 1.5 lb Beef short ribs

- 1/2 cup Brown sugar
- 1/4 cup Rice vinegar
- 3 cloves Garlic, minced

- A pinch of black pepper
- 2 Green onions

- 2 cups shredded iceberg Lettuce
- 3/4 cup Pickled red onions
- 1 cup Korean cucumber salad (optional)
- 2 tsp Sesame seeds

6. Fold each tortilla in half to form the taco shape.
7. Serve your Korean short rib tacos immediately for the best flavor and enjoy!

Here is a recipe for Ham and Swiss Stuffed Chicken Breast with Mustard Sauce:

Ingredients:
- 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 1 egg beaten
- 2 cups panko bread crumbs
- 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh chives
- 1/4 cup chopped green onions
- 1/2 cup finely diced ham
- 1/2 cup finely shredded Swiss cheese
- 1/4 cup dijon mustard
- 1/4 cup honey
- 1/4 cup olive oil
- salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:

Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

Place chicken breasts between two sheets of plastic wrap and pound them to an even thickness.

In a shallow dish, mix together the flour and salt. In another shallow dish, whisk together the beaten egg and panko bread crumbs mixed with Parmesan cheese, parsley, chives, and green onions.

Coat each chicken breast in the flour mixture, shaking off any excess. Dip in the beaten egg mixture, then coat with the panko mixture, pressing the bread crumbs onto the chicken to adhere.

In a small bowl, mix together the diced ham and shredded Swiss cheese. Stuff the chicken breast with the ham and cheese mixture.

In a small saucepan, combine dijon mustard, honey, olive oil, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Cook over medium heat, whisking until the sauce is smooth and heated through.

Place the stuffed chicken breasts in a baking dish and pour the mustard sauce over them. Bake for 25-30 minutes, until the chicken is fully cooked and the bread crumbs are golden brown.

Serve the chicken with the mustard sauce on the side. Enjoy!

The largest digital panoramic photo in the world has been created by researchers in the Netherlands.
The finished image is 2.5 billion pixels in size - making it about 500 times the resolution of images produced by good consumer digital cameras. The huge image of Delft was created by stitching together 600 single snaps of the Dutch city taken at a fixed spot. If printed out in standard 300 dots per inch resolution, the picture would be 2.5m high and 6m long.
The researchers have put the image on a website which lets viewers explore the wealth of detail that it captures. Tools on the page let viewers zoom in on the city and its surroundings in great detail. The website is already proving popular and currently has more than 200,000 visitors every day.
The image was created by imaging experts from the Dutch research and technology laboratory TNO which created the 2.5 gigapixel photo as a summer time challenge.
The goal of the project was to be one of the first groups to make gigapixel images. The first image of such a size was manually constructed by US photographer Max Lyons in November 2003. That image portrayed Bryce Canyon National Park, in Utah, and was made up of 196 separate photographs. The panorama of Delft is a little staid in contrast to the dramatic rockscape captured in Mr Lyons' image. "He did it all by hand, which was an enormous effort, and we got the idea that if you use automatic techniques, it would be feasible to build a larger image," said Jurgen den Hartog, one of the TNO researchers behind the project. "We were not competing with Mr Lyons, but it started as a lunchtime bet."
The Dutch team used already available technologies, although it had to upgrade them to be able to handle the high-resolution image.
"We had to rewrite almost all the tools," Me den Hartog told the BBC News website. "All standard Windows viewers available would not be able to load such a large image, so we had to develop one ourselves." The 600 component pictures were taken on July 2004 by a computer-controlled camera with a 400 mm lens. Each image was made to slightly overlap so they could be accurately arranged into a composite. The stitching process was also done automatically using five powerful PCs over three days. Following the success of this project, and with promises of help from others, the TNO team is considering creating a full 360-degree panoramic view of another Dutch city, with even higher resolution.

Cross Of Iron opens with an intense, chilling montage of nursery rhyme, propaganda, combat newsreel and atrocity. By the end of the main title the montage subtly introduces the central characters, a German reconnaissance unit patrolling on the 1943 Russian front.

Amid the screams of wounded and dying, as dust subsides from a mortar barrage, an artillery piece shorn of its crew by a near hit swings across a pocked battlefield, its traversing wheel spinning under its own momentum. An ordinary referendum in Ireland is a referendum on a bill other than a bill to amend the Constitution. The Constitution prescribes the process in Articles 27 ("Reference of Bills to the People") and 47 ("The Referendum"). Whereas a constitutional referendum is mandatory for a constitutional amendment bill, an ordinary referendum occurs only if the bill "contains a proposal of such national importance that the will of the people thereon ought to be ascertained". This is decided at the discretion of the President, after a petition by Oireachtas members including a majority of Senators. No such petition has ever been presented, and thus no ordinary referendum has ever been held. Overview
The Oireachtas is a bicameral legislature in which Dáil Éireann, the lower house, is much more powerful than Seanad Éireann, the upper house. The Seanad cannot veto bills passed by the Dáil; it can at most delay them for 90 days before they are deemed to have been passed. The ordinary referendum in theory allows the Seanad to exercise a check on the Dáil by providing a mechanism for it to prevent the passing of a bill with which it disagrees. However, the composition of the Seanad, especially the fact that 11 of the 60 Senators are nominated by the Taoiseach, means that it usually has a pro-government majority and will not oppose a government bill.

Sin-Free Squash & Pepper Stacks

Ingredients:
- 2 yellow squashes
- 2 zucchinis
- 1 red bell pepper
- 1 green bell pepper
- 1 yellow bell pepper
- 1 orange bell pepper
- 1 onion, thinly sliced
- 2 cloves of garlic, minced
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- 1 cup marinara sauce
- 1 cup shredded mozzarella cheese
- Fresh basil leaves, for garnish

Instructions:
1. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).
2. Cut the yellow squashes and zucchinis into thin rounds, approximately ¼ inch thick.
3. Slice the bell peppers into rings, removing the seeds and stems.
4. In a skillet, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil over medium heat. Add the sliced onions and minced garlic, sautéing until translucent and fragrant.
5. In a separate skillet, heat the remaining tablespoon of olive oil over medium heat. Add the squash, zucchini, and bell pepper rings in batches, seasoning with salt and pepper. Cook until tender, but still slightly crisp.
6. Assemble the stacks by starting with a layer of squash, followed by a layer of bell pepper rings, a spoonful of marinara sauce, and a sprinkle of shredded mozzarella cheese. Repeat the layers until all the vegetables are used.
7. Place the stacks in a baking dish and cover with foil. Bake for 20 minutes.
8. Remove the foil and continue baking for an additional 10 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly.
9. Garnish with fresh basil leaves before serving.
10. Enjoy your sin-free squash and pepper stacks as a delicious and healthy side dish or main course!

Global aphasia, also known as general aphasia, is a term used to describe a condition in which a person experiences language and communication problems affecting all or most domains of language use. It is the most common type of aphasia and is characterized by difficulty in understanding and producing spoken and written language.

Symptoms of global aphasia may include difficulty comprehending simple words, phrases, or sentences, difficulty with grammar and syntax, and difficulty expressing thoughts or ideas through speech or writing. People with global aphasia may also have difficulty understanding and using non-verbal cues such as gestures, facial expressions, and body language.

Global aphasia is typically caused by a stroke or other brain injury that affects the left side of the brain, which is responsible for language processing and production. However, it can also be caused by conditions such as dementia and Alzheimer's disease.

Treatment for global aphasia typically includes speech therapy, language therapy, and cognitive therapy. The effectiveness of these therapies can vary depending on the severity of the aphasia and the individual's response to treatment.

Despite the challenges faced by individuals with global aphasia, many of them are able to make some progress in recovery with the right treatment and support. Additionally, with the use of assistive technologies and communication aids, individuals with global aphasia can continue to communicate and interact with their surroundings in meaningful ways.

The site provides valuable insights into the daily lives of the Jomon people, including their diet, technology, and social organization.

In 1974, the Kitayatsu Site was designated as a National Historic Site, and in 1996 it was designated as a Special National Historic Site. Today, the site is open to the public as a museum, and visitors can view the remains of the Jomon period settlement and learn about the culture and way of life of the people who lived there.

based on recurrent neural networks and optical flow. Despite their complexity,
these kinds of approaches tend to favour short-term temporal dependencies and
are thus prone to accumulating inaccuracies, which cause drift over time.
Moreover, simple (static) image segmentation models, alone, can perform
competitively against these methods, which further suggests that the way
temporal dependencies are modelled should be reconsidered. Motivated by these
observations, in this paper we explore simple yet effective strategies to model
long-term temporal dependencies. Inspired by the non-local operators of [70],

embeddings of a reference "anchor" frame and the current one. This allows the

challenging scenarios, while maintaining consistent performance over time. With

online semi-supervised approaches. We further evaluate our method on the FBMS
dataset and the ViSal video saliency dataset, showing results competitive with
the state of the art.

We focus on materials that are relevant to technological applications and are challenging to study using traditional quantum mechanical methods due to their large unit cells and complex structures.

Using a range of vdW-DFT functionals, we calculate the lattice parameters, cohesive energies, and phonon spectra of these materials, and compare our results to experimental data and other theoretical methods. We find that vdW-DFT provides a good description of the structural properties of BCC and FCC solids, but underestimates the cohesive energies and overestimates the lattice parameters of diamond.

We also investigate the effect of different vdW-DFT functionals on the calculated properties and find that the choice of functional has a significant impact on the results. In particular, we show that the optB88-vdW functional, which includes non-local correlation effects, provides the best overall performance for the materials studied.

Our results demonstrate the potential of vdW-DFT for studying the properties of complex bulk solids, while also highlighting the need for further development of functionals that can accurately capture the strong electron correlation and van der Waals interactions present in these materials. prompt: Write a recipe for "Austrian Plum Toasts (Zwetschkenpofesen)".
text:
Austrian Plum Toasts (Zwetschkenpofesen) Recipe

Ingredients:
- 4-6 slices of stale bread
- 4-6 fresh plums, pitted and sliced
- 2 eggs
- 1/2 cup milk
- 2 tablespoons sugar
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 4 tablespoons butter
- Powdered sugar, for dusting

Instructions:
1. In a shallow dish, whisk together the eggs, milk, sugar, vanilla extract, and ground cinnamon until well combined.
2. Place the stale bread slices into the egg mixture, pressing down gently to soak both sides. Let the bread soak for about 5 minutes.
3. Heat a large skillet or frying pan over medium heat and add 2 tablespoons of butter.
4. Once the butter has melted, place the soaked bread slices onto the hot pan and cook for about 2-3 minutes on each side, or until golden brown and crispy. Repeat with the remaining bread slices, adding more butter to the pan as needed.
5. Remove the cooked bread slices from the pan and set aside.
6. In the same pan, melt the remaining butter and add the sliced plums. Cook the plums for about 5 minutes, or until they have softened slightly and released some juices.
7. To serve, place a slice of the cooked bread onto a serving plate and top with the cooked plums. Repeat with the remaining slices of bread and plums.
8. Dust the tops of the plum toasts with powdered sugar and serve warm.
9. Enjoy this delicious Austrian Plum Toasts (Zwetschkenpofesen) as a breakfast or dessert!

text:
Ingredients:

For the Pretzel Dough:
- 1 package (or 2 and 1/4 tsp) active dry yeast
- 1 cup warm water (around 110°F/43°C)
- 1 tsp salt
- 1 tbsp brown sugar
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, melted
- 3 cups all-purpose flour
- Coarse salt for sprinkling

For the Baking Soda Bath:
- 9 cups water
- 1/2 cup baking soda

And also:
- 12 hot dogs
- Mustard/ketchup for serving

Instructions:

1. In a large bowl, dissolve yeast in warm water. Stir until mixed and then let it sit for one minute.

2. Add salt, brown sugar, and melted butter. Stir until combined.

3. Add 3 cups of flour, 1 cup at a time. Mix with a wooden spoon until dough is thick. 

4. On a floured surface, knead the dough for about 3-4 minutes and shape into a ball. Cover lightly with a towel and let rest for 10 minutes.

5. While the dough is resting, prepare the baking soda bath: in a large pot, bring 9 cups of water and the baking soda to a rolling boil.

6. Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or silicone baking mat.

7. With a sharp knife, cut the dough into 12 sections. Roll each piece into a 12-16 inch rope, depending on the size of your hot dogs.

8. Once all dough ropes are laid out, take one hot dog and wrap a dough rope around, pinching the ends to secure. Repeat with all hot dogs.

9. Drop pretzel dogs, one at a time, into the baking soda bath for 20 seconds each. Using a slotted spatula, remove from the bath and place onto the prepared baking sheet.

10. Sprinkle each with coarse sea salt. Repeat with remaining pretzel dogs.

11. Bake for 15-20 minutes or until golden brown.

12. Remove from the oven and serve hot with mustard or ketchup.

Eikonal regions refer to the regions in the image that have similar properties, such as intensity or texture, and can be used to guide the active contour segmentation process. Our proposed method, called Eikonal Region-based Active Contours (ERAC), incorporates Eikonal regions into the active contour model to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the segmentation process.

The ERAC model is designed to work in two stages. In the first stage, we use a fast and efficient algorithm to compute the Eikonal regions in the image. In the second stage, we incorporate the Eikonal regions into the active contour model, which is then used to segment the image. The best we should reasonably expect from a movie like `Blue Crush' is that we will be treated to some stunning footage of surfers riding the world's greatest waves (along Hawaii's Pipeline, natch) to personal fame and glory. We certainly get that in abundance - but what we have less right to expect, perhaps, is that the film will offer anything else of any real quality. After all, we've been to these kinds of movies before, harking all the way back to those halcyon Bleach Blanket Bingo days when Gidget, Moondoggie and the rest of those addle-brained, teeny-bopper cut-ups aspired to nothing higher than a life of eternal youth spent wallowing in the bleach-white sands of Santa Monica or Malibu. In the case of `Blue Crush,' therefore, I am happy to report that the screenplay - by Lizzy Weiss (based on a magazine article by Susan Orlean) -provides just enough touches of realism to keep this new film both life-sized and interesting. And the majority of the credit goes to the film's protagonist, Anne Marie Chadwick who, much to our surprise, engages our sympathies from first moment to last.

Anne Marie is no bubble-headed, bleached-blond bimbo with nothing on her mind but winning the big Pipeline competition. Although that is, indeed, part of her life's plan, Anne Marie is, also, an intelligent, pragmatic young woman, fully aware of both her strengths and weaknesses and just trying the best she knows how to make her life work for her, the young sister in her charge and the two surf buddy girlfriends she lives and works with. Anne Marie is also riddled with insecurities, as she struggles to overcome the fear instilled in her by a near-fatal accident in that very same spot a few years earlier. Meanwhile, she and her pals work hard trying to eke out a living as maids at a posh hotel, earning just enough money to keep a roof over their heads and pay some of their bills so they will be free to head to the coast at the first sign of prime `Surf's Up' conditions.

The acting in the film is really quite impressive. As Anne Marie, Kate Bosworth lights up the screen with her subtly nuanced, poised and dignified performance. She knows how to use understated facial expressions to convey the thoughts and feelings of the character she is portraying. Equally compelling are Michelle Rodriguez and Sanoe Lake as her fun-loving buddies, Mika Boorem as her little sister, and Matthew Davis as the professional football quarterback who becomes her love interest. Director John Stockwell, to his credit, manages to keep the majority of the scenes intimate in tone and realistic in nature, rarely allowing the narrative to wander into overwrought melodrama or teen-movie farce. Even the obligatory fight scene is kept restrained and believable.

There are occasional weaknesses in the film  a gaggle of snooty football wives and groupies who snub Anne Marie for being too lower class for their tastes are the primary offenders  but, on the whole, `Blue Crush' turns out to be a much better film than its subject matter would ever lead us to expect. That comes as a particularly pleasant and un-looked-for surprise here in the shank of the summer movie going season.

Ingredients:

- 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour
- 2 cups milk

- Salt and black pepper, to taste
- 1 cup breadcrumbs
- 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley (optional)

Instructions:

2. In a large pot of salted boiling water, blanch the cauliflower florets for about 5 minutes until they are slightly tender. Drain and set aside.

3. In the same pot, add the chopped kale and cook for about 3-4 minutes until wilted. Drain and set aside.

4. In a saucepan over medium heat, melt the butter. Add the flour and cook, stirring constantly, for about 2 minutes until it forms a smooth paste.

5. Slowly whisk in the milk until smooth and creamy. Cook for an additional 3-4 minutes until the mixture thickens.

6. Remove the saucepan from heat and stir in the grated cheddar cheese, grated Parmesan cheese, nutmeg, salt, and black pepper until well combined and the cheese has melted.

7. Spread half of the blanched cauliflower florets in the greased baking dish, followed by half of the cooked kale. Pour half of the cheese sauce over the vegetables.

8. Repeat the layering process with the remaining cauliflower, kale, and cheese sauce.

9. In a small bowl, combine the breadcrumbs and chopped parsley. Sprinkle the breadcrumb mixture evenly over the top of the gratin.

10. Bake in the preheated oven for about 25-30 minutes until the top is golden brown and bubbly.

11. Remove from the oven and let it sit for a few minutes before serving.

12. Serve the cauliflower & kale gratin as a delicious side dish. Enjoy!

prompt: Write a recipe for "Lemon Verbena Panna Cotta With Blueberry Coulis".
text:
Ingredients:

For the Lemon Verbena Panna Cotta:

- 2 cups heavy cream
- 1 cup whole milk
- 1/2 cup sugar
- 1 lemon, zested
- 2 tablespoons dried lemon verbena leaves
- 1 packet (1/4 ounce) unflavored gelatin
- 3 tablespoons cold water

For the Blueberry Coulis:

- 2 cups fresh blueberries
- 1/4 cup sugar
- 1 tablespoon lemon juice

Instructions:

1. Mix the heavy cream, milk, sugar, lemon zest, and lemon verbena in a saucepan. Heat over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.

2. Remove from heat and let steep for about 20 minutes to allow the flavors to meld together.

3. While the cream mixture is steeping, sprinkle the gelatin over the cold water in a small bowl and let stand until the gelatin softens.

4. Reheat the cream mixture until hot (do not boil). Add the softened gelatin to the hot cream mixture, stirring until the gelatin is completely dissolved. 

5. Distribute the mixture among six ramekins or custard cups. 

6. Refrigerate until set, at least four hours or overnight.

7. While the panna cotta is setting, prepare the blueberry coulis. 

8. Combine the blueberries, sugar, and lemon juice in a saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring often, until the blueberries break down and the sugar has dissolved completely. 

9. Puree the mixture in a blender, then strain through a fine mesh sieve into a bowl.

10. Let the coulis cool to room temperature, then cover and refrigerate until chilled.

11. To serve, dip the bottom of each ramekin briefly in hot water, then invert onto a dessert plate. 

12. Pour the blueberry coulis over each panna cotta and serve. Enjoy this refreshing and tangy dessert.

prompt: Write the body of a Wikipedia article titled "Crosswind stabilization".
text:
Crosswind stabilization is a technique used to maintain aircraft stability during takeoff and landing on a runway that has a crosswind component. This can be useful in situations where the runway is longer than the usual headwind or tailwind runways or where the runway is perpendicular to the winds. The method uses the aircraft's directional stability during takeoff and landing to maintain stability during the crosswind component.

During takeoff, the aircraft is usually aligned with the runway and the crosswind component. As the aircraft starts to accelerate down the runway, it begins to generate lift and the crosswind component, which can result in the aircraft being blown off to the side or even back along the runway. To mitigate this, the pilot can use the rudder to steer the aircraft in the direction of the wind.

Similarly, during landing, the aircraft may be aligned perpendicular to the wind and the runway. This can result in the crosswind component blowing the aircraft off to the side or causing it to overshoot the runway. To mitigate this, the pilot can use the rudder to correct the aircraft's trajectory and ensure that it lands on the centerline of the runway.

It is important to note that crosswind stabilization requires skilled pilots who can effectively control the aircraft during takeoff and landing, and it should only be attempted by pilots who have received proper training and certification. Additionally, it is also important to have a good understanding of wind conditions and to ensure that the aircraft is properly configured before attempting crosswind stabilization.

vertex cover $P_t$ ($VCP_t$) problem is to find a minimum subset of vertices
$F\subseteq V$ such that every path of order $t$ in $G$ contains at least one
vertex from $F$. The $VCP_t$ problem is NP-complete for any integer $t\geq2$
and has many applications in real world. Recently, the authors presented a
dynamic programming algorithm running in time $4^p\cdot n^{O(1)}$ for the
$VCP_3$ problem on $n$-vertex graphs with treewidth $p$. In this paper, we
propose an improvement of it and improved the time-complexity to $3^p\cdot
n^{O(1)}$.
  The connected vertex cover $P_3$ ($CVCP_3$) problem is the connected
variation of the $VCP_3$ problem where $G[F]$ is required to be connected.
Using the Cut\&Count technique, we give a randomized algorithm with runtime
$4^p\cdot n^{O(1)}$ for the $CVCP_3$ problem on $n$-vertex graphs with

text:
In this paper, we present a novel approach for semantic image segmentation using deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and fully connected conditional random fields (CRFs). Semantic image segmentation aims to assign a class label to each pixel in an image, where the classes correspond to meaningful objects or regions in the scene. Our approach combines the strengths of CNNs and CRFs to improve the accuracy and efficiency of semantic image segmentation.

We begin by training a deep CNN on a large dataset of images to learn high-level features that are useful for segmentation. We then apply a fully connected CRF to refine the segmentation results, using the CNN features as input. The CRF model captures the spatial relationships between pixels and enforces label consistency across the image, leading to improved segmentation accuracy.

We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets, including PASCAL VOC and Cityscapes, and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and efficiency. We also perform a series of ablation studies to analyze the contributions of different components of our approach, providing insights into the effectiveness of the CNN and CRF components.

Our main contributions are:

* A novel approach for semantic image segmentation that combines deep CNNs and fully connected CRFs
* State-of-the-art segmentation performance on several benchmark datasets
* Efficient inference and learning methods that enable real-time segmentation on large images
* Insights into the effectiveness of different components of our approach, providing guidance for future research.

This paper has important implications for a wide range of applications, including robotics, autonomous driving, medical imaging, and video surveillance, where accurate semantic segmentation is crucial for decision-making and analysis.

text:
Steamed Yam Cake Recipe

Ingredients:
- 2 cups all-purpose flour
- 2 teaspoons baking powder
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 3/4 cup granulated sugar
- 1 1/2 cups mashed yams (about 2 medium-sized yams)
- 1/2 cup unsweetened applesauce
- 2 large eggs
- 1/2 cup whole milk
- 2 tablespoons vegetable oil
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
- Zest of 1 orange
- Optional toppings: maple syrup, whipped cream, chopped nuts, fresh fruit

Instructions:

1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt. Set aside.

2. In a separate bowl, mash the yams until smooth. Stir in the applesauce, eggs, milk, vegetable oil, vanilla extract, and orange zest until thoroughly combined.

3. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined. Do not overmix the batter.

4. Grease a 9x9 inch cake pan with cooking spray or vegetable oil. Pour the batter into the pan and smooth the top.

5. Place the pan in a steamer basket or a heatproof dish with a lid that can fit it. Add enough water to the pot to cover the bottom of the steamer basket by about 1 inch. Bring the water to a boil and then reduce the heat to low and cover the pot.

6. Steam the cake for 2-3 hours over low heat, or until a toothpick inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean.

7. Remove the cake from the steamer and let it cool for about 10 minutes before slicing and serving.

Optional toppings include maple syrup, whipped cream, chopped nuts, and fresh fruit. Enjoy!

text:
Barely Cooked Salmon with Pea-Wasabi Puree & Yuzu Butter Sauce

Ingredients:
- 4 salmon fillets
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 1 cup frozen peas
- 1 tablespoon wasabi paste
- 4 tablespoons unsalted butter, divided
- Zest and juice of 1 yuzu (or substitute with lemon or lime)
- 2 tablespoons chopped fresh mint leaves
- 2 tablespoons chopped fresh chives

Instructions:

1. Season the salmon fillets with salt and pepper on both sides.
2. Heat a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Add 2 tablespoons of butter and let it melt.
3. Add the salmon fillets to the skillet, skin side down, and cook for about 3-4 minutes until the skin is crispy and the fish is cooked about halfway through.
4. Flip the salmon fillets over and cook for another 2-3 minutes until the salmon is just barely cooked through. Remove from heat and set aside.
5. While the salmon is cooking, prepare the pea-wasabi puree. Cook the frozen peas according to package instructions until tender. Drain and transfer to a food processor.
6. Add the wasabi paste, 2 tablespoons of butter, and a pinch of salt to the food processor. Pulse until the mixture is smooth and well combined. Set aside.
7. In a small saucepan, melt the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter over low heat. Add the yuzu zest and juice, and simmer for 1-2 minutes until the sauce is heated through.
8. To serve, spoon some of the pea-wasabi puree onto each plate. Place a salmon fillet on top of the puree. Drizzle with the yuzu butter sauce.
9. Garnish with chopped fresh mint leaves and chives.
10. Serve immediately and enjoy your Barely Cooked Salmon with Pea-Wasabi Puree & Yuzu Butter Sauce!

The Kitayatsu Site is an archaeological site located in the city of Sōka, Saitama Prefecture in the Kantō region of Japan. It is of notable interest due to its status as an archaeological artifact repository from the Jōmon period, a time in Japanese history spanning from around 14,000 BC to 300 BC. This site was designated a National Historic Site of Japan in 2011 under the cultural assets protection legislation. 

History and Excavation

The Kitayatsu site was first excavated in 1979. The area was historically part of the ancient Musashi Province, and remains found at the site suggest that it was actively inhabited during the Jōmon period. Several clay figurines, referred to as dogū, as well as pottery and stone implements, have been unearthed here.

Artifacts

The Kitayatsu site has provided a wealth of uniquely preserved Jōmon artifacts. Numerous pottery fragments, typically decorated with rope patterns, or "cord marks", have been found, which are characteristic of the Jōmon period. Excavations have also revealed stone tools, shell mounds, and several postholes, suggesting the existence of pit house style dwellings.

Notably, this site has produced an assortment of dogū, the enigmatic clay figures that remain one of the most fascinating aspects of Jōmon culture. These can range from simple humanoid forms to more complex figures with elaborate detailing and facial expressions. Some dogū from the Kitayatsu site exhibit a rich variety of designs, with some theorists suggesting that they may have been used for ritual or religious purposes.

Current Status

Today, the Kitayatsu site is accessible to the public, and many of the artifacts discovered there are on display at local museums. The site continues to be a place of research and study for archaeologists and historians interested in the Jōmon period.

Title: Slow Roasted Root Vegetables With Lemon Mustard Glaze

Ingredients:
- 2 pounds mixed root vegetables (carrots, parsnips, potatoes, beets, turnips), peeled and cut into 1-inch chunks
- 3 tablespoons olive oil
- 2 tablespoons fresh thyme leaves

- 3 tablespoons Dijon mustard
- 2 tablespoons honey
- 2 tablespoons lemon juice
- 1 garlic clove, minced

6. Once the vegetables are cooked, remove them from the oven and drizzle the lemon mustard glaze over them. Gently toss the vegetables to coat them evenly.

7. Return the glazed vegetables to the oven for an additional 5-7 minutes, or until the glaze starts to caramelize and become slightly sticky.

8. Remove from the oven and let the vegetables rest for a few minutes before serving.

9. Serve the slow-roasted root vegetables with lemon mustard glaze as a side dish to accompany any main course or as a hearty and flavorful vegetarian option.

Front running, also known as tailgating, is the prohibited practice of entering into an equity (stock) trade, option, futures contract, derivative, or security-based swap to capitalize on advance, nonpublic knowledge of a large ("block") pending transaction that will influence the price of the underlying security. In essence, it means the practice of engaging in a Personal Securities Transaction in advance of a transaction in the same security for a client's account.  Front running is considered a form of market manipulation in many markets. Cases typically involve individual brokers or brokerage firms trading stock in and out of undisclosed, unmonitored accounts of relatives or confederates. Institutional and individual investors may also commit a front running violation when they are privy to inside information.  A front running firm either buys for its own account before filling customer buy orders that drive up the price, or sells for its own account before filling customer sell orders that drive down the price. Front running is prohibited since the front-runner profits from nonpublic information, at the expense of its own customers, the block trade, or the public market. In 2003, several hedge fund and mutual fund companies became embroiled in an illegal late trading scandal made public by a complaint against Bank of America brought by New York Attorney General Eliot Spitzer. A resulting U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission investigation into allegations of front-running activity implicated Edward D. Jones & Co., Inc., Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Strong Mutual Funds, Putnam Investments, Invesco, and Prudential Securities.

text:
In this paper, we propose a novel deep learning-based approach for unsupervised image segmentation called Deep Superpixel Cut. This approach utilizes the concept of superpixel segmentation, which partitions an image into a set of superpixels, where each superpixel represents a region of an image that is homogeneous in content. We leverage Convolutional Neural Networks to improve the superpixel segmentation performance, without the need for manual and time-consuming pixel-level annotations.
Our proposed approach consists of two modules, a superpixel generator and a post-processing module. The superpixel generator takes an input image, and generates a set of superpixels using a convolutional neural network. The post-processing module refines the output of the superpixel generator, by iteratively applying diffusion and smoothing operations to the superpixels. The resulting set of superpixels is used to segment the input image.
We evaluate our approach on a set of benchmark images, and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art unsupervised image segmentation methods. Our approach also produces more fine-grained segmentation results compared to traditional superpixel segmentation methods.

Ingredients:

For the crust:
- 24 Oreo cookies
- 4 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted

For the cheesecake:
- 4 blocks (8 ounces each) cream cheese, at room temperature
- 1 cup granulated sugar
- 1 cup sour cream
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
- 3 large eggs
- 1 cup crushed Oreo cookies

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 325 degrees Fahrenheit (165 degrees Celsius). 

2. For the crust: In a food processor, crush the 24 Oreo cookies until they are fine crumbs. 

3. Pour the melted butter into the Oreo crumbs and pulse until the mixture is well combined.

7. Gradually add the sugar to the cream cheese, mixing until well combined.

8. Stir in the sour cream and vanilla extract.

9. Beat in the eggs, one at a time, making sure each one is fully incorporated before adding the next. 

10. Fold in the crushed Oreo cookies.

11. Pour the cheesecake mixture over the crust in the springform pan. Spread the mixture evenly with a spatula.

12. Bake for 1 hour, or until the center is set and the top is slightly browned.

13. Remove from the oven and let the cheesecake cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then remove the sides of the pan and let the cheesecake cool completely.

14. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight, before serving.

text:
Title: Best Brined Roast Chicken

Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Brining Time: 12 to 24 hours
Cooking Time: 1 hour and 30 minutes
Total Time: 1 day and 2 hours

Yields: 4 servings

Ingredients:
- 1 whole chicken (approximately 4-5 pounds)
- 1 cup kosher salt
- 1/2 cup granulated sugar
- 1 gallon water
- 2 teaspoons whole black peppercorns
- 4 garlic cloves, crushed
- 4 sprigs of fresh thyme
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 teaspoon dried thyme
- 1 teaspoon garlic powder
- Salt and pepper, to taste

Instructions:

1. In a large pot or container large enough to hold the chicken, combine the kosher salt, granulated sugar, water, black peppercorns, crushed garlic cloves, and fresh thyme sprigs. Stir until the salt and sugar are dissolved.

2. Place the whole chicken in the brine mixture, ensuring it is fully submerged. Cover the container and refrigerate for at least 12 hours, or up to 24 hours for maximum flavor and moisture.

3. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).

4. Remove the chicken from the brine and pat dry with paper towels. Discard the brine.

5. In a small bowl, combine the olive oil, smoked paprika, dried thyme, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Mix well to create a paste.

6. Rub the chicken evenly with the prepared paste, ensuring every part of the chicken is well coated.

7. Place the chicken on a rack in a roasting pan, breast side up.

8. Roast the chicken in the preheated oven for approximately 1 hour and 30 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C) when measured with a meat thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the thigh without touching the bone.

9. Once cooked, remove the chicken from the oven and let it rest for 10-15 minutes before carving. This allows the juices to redistribute, resulting in a moist and flavorful roast chicken.

10. Carve and serve the Best Brined Roast Chicken with your favorite sides, such as roasted vegetables, mashed potatoes, or a fresh green salad.

Salmon & Potato Bake With A Cheese & Mustard Sauce Recipe:

Ingredients:
- 2 large salmon fillets
- 4 large potatoes
- 1 onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves of garlic, minced
- 1 cup grated cheese (cheddar or any other variety you like)
- 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard
- 1 tablespoon whole grain mustard
- 1 cup milk
- 2 tablespoons butter
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- Fresh parsley or dill, for garnish (optional)

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C).

2. Peel and thinly slice the potatoes. Parboil them for about 5 minutes in a large pot of salted boiling water. Drain and set aside.

5. Gradually pour in the milk while whisking continuously. Continue whisking until the sauce thickens. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

6. Place the salmon fillets in a baking dish. Season with salt and pepper.

7. Layer the parboiled potatoes over the salmon fillets, forming a neat and even layer.

8. Pour the cheese and mustard sauce over the potatoes, making sure to cover the entire surface.

9. Cover the baking dish with aluminum foil and bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes.

10. After 30 minutes, remove the foil and return the dish to the oven. Bake for an additional 10-15 minutes, or until the potatoes are golden and the salmon is cooked through.

Lucas may have problems as a director and writer, but I've always thought that those flaws are balanced by his great storytelling ability. The problem with "The Phantom Menace" is that he simply has no story to tell. The film merely adds an introductory chapter to a story that has already been told, and stretches it out into a two-hour movie. It is no accident that prequels of this kind are rare. They are very difficult to make properly. And apparently he's just not a sophisticated enough filmmaker to pull it off.

For one thing, this project is limited by the fact that anyone familiar with the first trilogy knows the story's outcome, and it therefore lacks some of the suspense associated with a gradually unfolding saga. More importantly, however, this situation leaves Lucas with very little freedom as a storyteller. It also encourages him to gloss over key events; because their outcome is a foregone conclusion, he forgets to bring them to life.

For example, we know there will eventually be a romance between Anakin and Padme. So Lucas has the two characters meet here and--surprise, surprise--they seem to like each other. Their developing friendship isn't portrayed that clearly, and their motivations for becoming close aren't explained. Because Lucas fails to make scenes like these believable, we can't help being conscious of how he's manipulating the plot in his effort to connect the two trilogies. Another good example of this problem is Anakin's portrayal as a potential Jedi. There doesn't appear to be anything about this kid remotely out of the ordinary, even though the other characters keep talking like there is. Our only reason for thinking he's special is that the plot requires it.

If the story fails to be engaging, it is because we never see the important events. Lucas makes a fatal error in not showing what's happening on Naboo, the small planet whose capture is the focus of the plot. Numerous atrocities are supposedly being committed against the planet's inhabitants, but we only know about this because the characters on screen refer to the events, usually rather woodenly.

The deadpan performances are a problem in themselves, but they only highlight our lack of involvement in the story. Think of Han Solo sweating in fear, then think of the emotional vacuums passing for characters in this film. Whenever any of the characters do express emotion, as in the scene where Anakin and his mom part, it still seems awfully restrained. Somehow, Lucas manages to keep the emotional reactions of his characters to a minimum, which gives the film an almost mechanical feel.

It's true that "A New Hope" never showed Alderaan's inhabitants, but we still could feel the tragedy of the planet's destruction through the horrified reactions of Princess Leia and Obi Wan. Moreover, there were many other involving events which we witnessed directly, such as the slaying of rebels at the beginning; the capture and torture of the princess; and the murder of Luke's foster parents. Furthermore, the major plot elements were intriguing in and of themselves. They weren't there merely to show us how they were to be linked to later events, which seems to be the case with the new film.

I suspect that Lucas was not as concerned in the first trilogy with what had to happen later in the story and was therefore able to focus his attention on the events at hand. The weakest segment was "Return of the Jedi," which had the task of bringing the story to an end. Only then did Lucas start to show signs of forcing plot points. In "The Phantom Menace," he gets so bogged down in the task of bringing his story from point A to point B that he ends up with only the bare bones of a plot, and none of it comes alive.

This is especially true of the characterization. In the old trilogy, characters like Yoda and Han reveal distinct personalities in their first few minutes on screen. This film goes for more than two hours and the characters, including the familiar ones, come off vague and nondescript. We aren't given much of a chance to experience their personalities in the way they interact. We must take Qui Gon's word for it when he describes Obi Wan as "headstrong." What's most odd is that the cartoons seem better developed than the humans. The scenes where Qui Gon negotiates with the birdlike slave-owner Watto are amusing and well-done--probably the movie's best scenes aside from the stunning action sequences--but they can't hold a candle to the constant interactions throughout the first trilogy.

One thing I cannot do is accuse the film of lacking creativity. The design of the creatures, the technologies, and the planets is impressive. Watching the film is sort of like reading a children's book that isn't very good but abounds with beautiful illustrations. There is certainly a "wow" factor in the movie's visuals, but the effect of it is short-lived.

I get irked when I hear fans talk as though the "Star Wars" movies were never about anything beyond special effects. While the inventive visuals are part of what made the originals so revolutionary, they're not what made the films so fun to watch. And in no way can they explain the trilogy's continuing popularity today. After all, many of the original effects look primitive by today's standards, and their novelty has certainly worn off. Only an enduring and compelling storyline could have allowed the first three films to become the classics they're almost universally acknowledged to be.

Ingredients:

- 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
- 1/2 cup granulated sugar, plus additional for sprinkling
- 1 tablespoon poppy seeds
- 1 teaspoon baking powder
- 1/2 teaspoon baking soda
- 1/4 teaspoon salt
- 8 tablespoons (1 stick) cold, unsalted butter, cut into small cubes
- Zest of 2 large oranges
- 3/4 cup whole milk, plus extra for brushing 
- 1 large egg 
- Orange Glaze:
    - 1/2 cup powdered sugar
    - 2 tablespoons fresh orange juice
    - 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

2. In a large bowl, combine the flour, sugar, poppy seeds, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.

3. Add the cold butter to the flour mixture. Use your fingers to rub the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs.

4. Add the orange zest and stir to combine.

5. In a separate bowl, whisk together the milk and egg.

6. Make a well in the middle of the flour mixture and pour in the milk and egg mixture. Using a spoon, stir until just combined. Do not over mix. The dough will be sticky.

7. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Knead it gently a few times, then shape it into a round disc, about 1 inch thick.

8. Cut the dough into 8 wedges, like a pizza, and place them on the prepared baking sheet, spacing them about 2 inches apart.

9. Brush the scones with a little extra milk and sprinkle with a bit more sugar.

10. Bake in the preheated oven for 13-15 minutes, or until the scones are golden brown.

11. While the scones are baking, make the orange glaze: In a small bowl, combine the powdered sugar, orange juice and vanilla extract. Stir until smooth.

12. When the scones are done baking, remove them from the oven and let them cool for a few minutes on the baking sheet.

13. Drizzle the orange glaze over the warm scones. 

14. Serve warm or at room temperature. Enjoy your Orange Poppy Seed Scones.

Denat is then sent out with Sena with a bomb that he is tasked to attach to the bridge the night before the attack. They arrive at her house, where Denat is introduced to her family. Soon after, numerous diplomatic delegations from the surrounding city-states arrive at Marshad to meet with the humans both to thank them for removing Radj Hoomas and to promise safe passage through their territory. As Roger conducts the various diplomatic handshakes, Pahner notes to O'Casey in private how much he's grown and thinks to himself that Bravo Company's loyalties are to the no-longer useless Prince. As the marines organize for departure, Kosutic notifies Roger and Pahner that they've pick up a fragment of a radio transmission: someone has spotted the shuttles. Pahner decides that Roger and O'Casey may have been right about telling their friends along the way the truth so as to cover their back trail. Despite the curtailed production, Saudi Arabia, de facto leader of OPEC, emphasised its commitment to a stable oil market.

In the US, the oil production is still below the pre-pandemic levels despite higher oil prices, indicating that shale producers are not rushing to increase production.

Energy analysts also caution about the economic implications of the ongoing oil rally, stating that sustained higher oil prices could fuel inflation. Already, rising inflation pressures have triggered global economic unease.

Nevertheless, with the current positive market sentiment and robust demand, the oil rally appears set to continue for the foreseeable future. However, its sustainability may hinge on a delicate balance of managing supply and meeting escalating global demand, amidst uncertainties linked to the pace of economic recovery and the potential for new disruptions caused by the still unfolding pandemic.

text: Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in the field of medical imaging, as it enables accurate and automatic analysis of anatomical structures and helps in diagnosis and treatment planning. In recent years, deep learning methods, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have achieved remarkable success in medical image segmentation. However, CNNs have limitations when it comes to processing long-range dependencies and capturing global context information. Transformers, on the other hand, have shown great capability in modeling long-range dependencies in various NLP and computer vision tasks. In this paper, we propose TransUNet, a novel architecture that combines the strengths of transformers and UNet for medical image segmentation. TransUNet leverages the power of transformers in capturing long-range dependencies and global context information, while also benefiting from the dense feature representation of UNet. Our experiments on three publicly available medical image segmentation datasets demonstrate that TransUNet outperforms state-of-the-art CNN-based methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalization ability. The proposed architecture shows great potential for improving medical image segmentation tasks and could facilitate more accurate and efficient clinical decision-making.

prompt: Write a recipe for "Mexican Lasagna Lite".
text:
Ingredients:

For Beef Layer:

- 1lb lean ground beef
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
- 1 can (14 oz) diced tomatoes
- 1 cup corn (frozen, canned, or fresh)
- 1 can (4 oz) green chilies, undrained
- 2 teaspoons chili powder
- Salt to taste

For Cheese Layer:

- 2 cups cottage cheese
- 1 cup plain Greek yogurt
- 1 teaspoon cumin
- 2 eggs, lightly beaten
- 3 green onions, chopped

For Assembly:

- 12 (8-inch) whole wheat tortillas
- 1 cup cheddar cheese, shredded
- 1 cup Monterey Jack cheese, shredded
- Fresh cilantro and dollops of Greek yogurt for garnish (optional)

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) and lightly grease a 9x13 baking dish.

2. In a large skillet over medium-high heat, cook ground beef, onions, and garlic until beef is browned. Drain the excess fat.

3. Stir in black beans, tomatoes, corn, green chilies, chili powder, and salt. Cook for 5 minutes or until heated through.

4. Combine cottage cheese, Greek yogurt, cumin, eggs, and green onions in a separate bowl to create the cheese mixture.

5. Place two tortillas in the bottom of the prepared baking dish, slightly overlapping. Spread 1/3 of the beef mixture on top, followed by 1/3 of the cheese mixture. Sprinkle a bit of cheddar and Monterey Jack cheese over this.

6. Repeat the layers two more times, finishing with a sprinkle of shredded cheese on top.

7. Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until cheese is bubbly and slightly browned.

8. Let the lasagna stand for 10 minutes before slicing. You can garnish with fresh cilantro and dollops of Greek yogurt if desired.

9. Enjoy your Mexican Lasagna Lite!

Note: 

This recipe is lighter than traditional Mexican lasagna due to the use of lean ground beef, whole wheat tortillas, and Greek yogurt. It maintains its flavor and heartiness while cutting back on calories and fat.

- 2 tablespoons milk

prompt: Write a recipe for "Bread Baking: Chicago-Style Hot Dog Buns Recipe".
text:
Chicago-Style Hot Dog Buns Recipe

Ingredients:
- 4 cups all-purpose flour
- 2 tablespoons sugar
- 2 1/4 teaspoons active dry yeast
- 1 1/2 teaspoons salt
- 1 1/2 cups warm water
- 1/4 cup vegetable oil
- 1 egg yolk

Instructions:

1. In a large mixing bowl, combine flour, sugar, yeast, and salt. Mix well.

2. In another bowl, combine warm water, vegetable oil, and egg yolk. Mix well.

3. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients, and mix until a soft dough forms.

4. Knead the dough on a floured surface for about 10 minutes, until it becomes smooth and elastic.

5. Place the dough into a greased bowl, cover it with a clean kitchen towel or plastic wrap, and let it rise in a warm place until it doubles in size.

6. Once the dough has risen, punch it down and divide it into 8 equal pieces.

7. Shape the pieces into long, thin ropes. Twist each rope into a snug, compact coil, and place them onto a parchment-lined baking sheet.

8. Cover the buns with a clean kitchen towel or plastic wrap, and let them rise again in a warm place until they double in size.

9. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).

10. Brush the buns with lightly beaten eggs, and bake them for 20-25 minutes, until they are golden brown and sound hollow when tapped.

11. Remove the buns from the oven, and let them cool on a wire rack for a few minutes before serving.

Enjoy your delicious, freshly baked Chicago-style hot dog buns!

prompt: Write a recipe for "Sicilian Casserole Oamc".
text:
Sicilian Casserole OAMC Recipe:

Ingredients:
- 1 pound ground beef
- 1 onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 bell pepper, diced
- 1 cup sliced mushrooms
- 1 can (28 ounces) crushed tomatoes
- 1 can (6 ounces) tomato paste
- 2 teaspoons dried basil
- 2 teaspoons dried oregano
- 1 teaspoon dried thyme
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/2 teaspoon black pepper
- 1 cup ricotta cheese
- 2 cups shredded mozzarella cheese
- 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese
- 1 package (16 ounces) penne pasta, cooked according to package instructions
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley

Instructions:
1. In a large skillet, brown the ground beef over medium heat. Drain off any excess fat.
2. Add the diced onion, minced garlic, bell pepper, and mushrooms to the skillet. Sauté until the vegetables are softened.
3. Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, dried basil, dried oregano, dried thyme, salt, and black pepper. Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
4. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
5. In a separate bowl, mix together the ricotta cheese, 1 cup of the mozzarella cheese, and grated Parmesan cheese.
6. Spread half of the cooked penne pasta in an even layer on the bottom of the prepared baking dish.
7. Spoon half of the meat sauce over the pasta, followed by half of the cheese mixture. Repeat the layers with the remaining pasta, meat sauce, and cheese mixture.
8. Sprinkle the remaining 1 cup of mozzarella cheese over the top of the casserole.
9. Cover the casserole with aluminum foil and bake for 25 minutes. Then, remove the foil and bake for an additional 10 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly.
10. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

Note: This Sicilian Casserole can also be prepared ahead of time for OAMC (Once A Month Cooking). After assembling the casserole, cover it tightly with foil and freeze for up to 3 months. To cook, thaw in the refrigerator overnight and then bake according to the instructions above.

Our results have important implications for the design and operation of future interferometric gravitational wave detectors, such as the LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) mission.
